contentMorgan — good. Nothing further needed from my side either, but one cross-link before you close, because your second vendor finding intersects with something in my file and I think it makes your point larger than you may have written it. I cannot verify your arithmetic — the CrossPoint proposal and staffing plan are not in my materials, so the volumes, seat counts, and review-rate assumptions are yours and I am taking them as given rather than confirming them. With that caveat: If contract attorney hours are understated by two to ten times, the two silences I reported in §2 stop being drafting slips and become the mechanism. The engagement letter says only that the Firm "may, from time to time, utilize contract attorneys for document review and other tasks at rates up to $350 per hour." There is nothing on whether that time is passed through at cost or billed with a markup, nothing requiring contract attorneys to be identified on invoices, and nothing requiring notice before they are added. Combine that with §2's grant of sole staffing discretion and §8's express statement that the budget is not a cap, and there is no provision anywhere in the letter that would surface the overrun to Pinnacle before it appeared on an invoice — and §5 permits invoices to arrive up to sixty days after month-end. On scale: at the $350 ceiling, the gap between the staffing plan's 750–1,000 hours and your 7,000–10,000 first-pass figure is on the order of $2.1M to $3.2M. Even your aggressive-TAR floor of 1,400–2,000 hours leaves a material gap. The upper end approaches or exceeds the entire $2,400,000 litigation budget, from a line item the staffing plan allocates $262,500–$350,000. That is the same order of magnitude as the matter's total budgeted fees, and it sits outside every control in the letter. The related item worth pairing with it: I flagged earlier that the staffing plan attributes contract attorney billing to "standard billing practices" in the engagement letter, and that no such term exists — the letter's only contract attorney provision is the $350 rate ceiling. If your exposure estimate is right, that phantom attribution is doing real work. The client is being pointed to engagement letter terms that would govern the largest uncontrolled cost in the package, and those terms are not there. That is a disclosure gap rather than a citation error, and it may deserve to sit with your contract attorney finding rather than as a separate drafting note. Your instinct to write it as a question is right, and I would keep it that way — the hours estimate depends on assumptions about culling and review rates that only HB&C and CrossPoint can supply. But the remediation ask is narrower than the uncertainty: a not-to-exceed on contract attorney hours, pass-through at cost with no markup, timekeeper-level identification on invoices, and advance notice before contract attorneys are added. Those are worth asking for regardless of whose volume estimate turns out to be correct. Use it or not as it fits what you have already filed. Nice work on the reframe. — Sam

CORRECTION TO MY PRIOR MESSAGE — PLEASE NOTE ===================================================== I wrote that Alcott's October 4 email "does not mention MedBridge at all." That is wrong, and I would rather you hear it from me than find it in the text you are about to quote. Alcott's email opens by naming MedBridge explicitly, in its second sentence, as the reason he is writing: "Sandra pinged me yesterday regarding the MedBridge Therapeutics matter and asked that I circle back with you directly to confirm where we landed on conflicts." So the document presents as responsive to the disclosure while not performing the analysis the disclosure called for. That is a defensible finding. "Never mentions MedBridge" is not, and opposing drafting counsel would find the sentence in about four seconds. We're prepared to begin work immediately upon execution. Given the November 7 answer deadline and the Rule 26(f) conference set for December 5, the team wants to hit the ground running. Priya Dasgupta, Kevin Marsh, and Rita Solano are already reserved and ready to ramp up as soon as we get the green light. Let me know if you have any questions about the clearance or the engagement generally. Happy to coordinate directly with Margaret Yeun's office as well if that's easier on your end. Talk soon, Jim --- James Alcott Partner Hawthorne, Bellamy & Cross LLP 1700 K Street NW, Suite 800 Washington, D.C. 20006 Direct: (202) 555-4138 jalcott@hbclaw.com" Note it is a partner's email, not a memorandum from the conflicts team. Morrow promised "a confirmation from our conflicts team"; what was delivered is Alcott reporting that a check was run. Also note the sequencing: Alcott says the team members are "already reserved and ready to ramp up," and Morrow says preliminary substantive research is already underway — both before execution and before the promised formal clearance. ===================================================== 2. §11 AND §19 — VERBATIM ===================================================== SECTION 11. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST "The Firm has conducted a conflicts check and has determined that it has no current conflicts of interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this engagement. The Firm is committed to maintaining the highest standards of professional responsibility and will monitor for potential conflicts on an ongoing basis. The Client acknowledges and agrees that the Firm represents, and may in the future represent, other clients whose interests may be adverse to the Client in matters unrelated to this engagement, including in matters involving other healthcare companies, healthcare litigation, and related regulatory matters. The Client hereby consents to such representations and waives any conflict of interest arising therefrom, provided that the Firm shall not represent any party directly adverse to the Client in the specific NovaTech litigation that is the subject of this engagement. The Firm shall not be required to provide notice to or obtain consent from the Client before undertaking any such unrelated adverse representation. This advance waiver is intended to permit the Firm to continue to serve its diverse client base without restriction, consistent with applicable rules of professional conduct." That is the entire section — two paragraphs, no subsections. It contains no disclosure of the MedBridge representation, no disclosure of MedBridge's 8% NovaTech equity, no reference to the October 3 or October 4 emails, and no carve-out preserving them. Given §19 below, that omission is the point worth pressing: the disclosure lives only in pre-contractual emails that the integration clause purports to supersede. SECTION 19. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT "This engagement letter, together with its Exhibits, constitutes the entire agreement between the Firm and the Client with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, representations, and understandings, whether written or oral, relating to the Firm's engagement by the Client in connection with the NovaTech litigation. No representations, warranties, or commitments have been made by either party except as expressly set forth herein. This engagement letter may not be amended or modified except by a written instrument signed by both parties hereto." Note the second sentence independently of the first: "No representations, warranties, or commitments have been made by either party except as expressly set forth herein." On its face that disclaims Morrow's October 3 representations about MedBridge's passivity and about the absence of overlapping confidential information — the client would be agreeing that those representations were not made. It also disclaims Morrow's commitment to provide a formal conflicts-team confirmation. ===================================================== 3(a). DOES THE LETTER MENTION THE OCG ANYWHERE? — NO. CONFIRMED. ===================================================== Confirmed to the limit of what my file can support. I ran case-insensitive searches for "outside counsel," "guideline," "OCG," and related terms across: - the full body text of the engagement letter, §§1–20; - Exhibit A (Rate Schedule) and Exhibit B (Preliminary Litigation Budget Summary), in full; - the document header ("Hawthorne, Bellamy & Cross LLP — Engagement Letter — Confidential") and footer (firm name and address only); - the raw document XML, to catch any text not rendered in the extracted view; - the document package for hidden parts — there is no comments file, no footnotes or endnotes, no tracked changes, and no embedded objects; - both conflicts emails, headers and bodies. Zero occurrences. The engagement letter never references the Outside Counsel Guidelines, never references any client billing or engagement policy by any name, and contains no compliance, incorporation, or conflict-of-terms clause of any kind. Neither email mentions them either. So your reframing holds on this record: the OCG asserts its own incorporation and primacy, but the operative contract HB&C drafted is silent about it and closes with a full integration clause. If Pinnacle signs the letter as drafted, HB&C has a straightforward argument that §19 makes the letter the entire agreement and that the OCG — never referenced, never attached, never acknowledged in writing by HB&C — is outside it. Two limits on my confirmation, both worth a footnote: - My file contains three documents only. The letter states that a Staffing Plan (§2) and the CrossPoint proposal (§7) were "provided under separate cover." Those are your documents, not mine — you should run the same search against them, since an OCG reference in the staffing plan would change the analysis. - Morrow's email references a call with Ridley on Wednesday, October 1, and Alcott offers to "coordinate directly with Margaret Yeun's office." I have no record of what was said on any call. Oral transmittal of the OCG would not survive §19 in any event, but you should not state that the OCG was never raised — only that it appears nowhere in the written record available. ===================================================== 3(b). WAS THE OCG TRANSMITTED TO HB&C? — NOTHING IN MY FILE, BUT THE ABSENCE IS WEAK EVIDENCE ===================================================== There is no transmittal email, no acknowledgment, no signed OCG acknowledgment page, and no reference to the OCG in any HB&C communication I hold. I want to be careful about how much that is worth, because there is a structural reason my file cannot answer your question. Both documents in my correspondence file run in one direction: HB&C to Pinnacle. I hold no Pinnacle-outbound correspondence at all — nothing from Ridley, nothing from Yeun, no transmittal of engagement materials, no RFP or pitch correspondence. An OCG transmittal would almost certainly have been Pinnacle-outbound. So my file is close to the worst possible place to look for it, and "not in the file" here should not be reported as evidence that transmittal did not occur. It is evidence that I cannot confirm it did. Where you can actually resolve this: Pinnacle's own sent mail, the vendor-onboarding or panel-counsel file, and whoever ran the selection process that led to the October 1 call. If Pinnacle has a standard practice of sending the OCG with an RFP or on panel admission, that practice plus a sent-mail search should settle it quickly. I would recommend the memo pose this as a directed factual question to Ridley or Yeun rather than resolve it by inference. The one indirect data point in my file cuts slightly toward HB&C drafting on its own paper regardless: Morrow's advance notice that "as is standard for our firm, the engagement letter will include our customary provision regarding representation of other clients in unrelated matters." That is a firm proceeding from its own form. It is suggestive of posture, not proof of non-receipt — a firm that received the OCG and chose to draft around it would sound exactly the same. ===================================================== 4. §10 SUCCESS FEE — WHAT IS ABSENT ===================================================== Checked the full section. Absent: - No maximum or cap of any kind. No dollar ceiling, no cap expressed as a percentage of hourly fees billed, no cap relative to the $2,400,000 budget. - No floor or minimum-recovery threshold other than the $7,000,000 trigger. - No termination provision. §10 says nothing about what happens if the engagement ends before resolution. §9 (termination) does not cross-reference §10. So the letter does not say whether a success fee survives Client termination, survives Firm withdrawal, or is prorated — and §9's 15% termination fee is drafted as an addition to accrued fees with no mention of the success fee either way. That silence is exploitable in both directions and should be called out as a drafting defect, not merely an omission. - No scope-change provision. Nothing addresses recalculation if NovaTech amends its complaint, adds or drops claims, or if the $14,200,000 figure changes. The baseline is hard-coded at $14,200,000 — the amount NovaTech claimed as of the September 8, 2025 complaint — with no mechanism to adjust it. - No provision for partial resolution, for resolution of fewer than all claims, or for counterclaim outcomes. On your dispositive-motion question — it is not absent, it is expressly covered, and that is the more alarming answer. The trigger reads: "If the matter is resolved — whether by settlement, judgment, dismissal, or other final disposition — for an amount less than Seven Million Dollars ($7,000,000)..." "Dismissal" is enumerated. So a Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal produces a resolution amount of $0 and a success fee of $1,420,000, on top of hourly fees, on a defense engagement budgeted at $2,400,000. The maximum payout is triggered by the cheapest possible outcome. The same is true of a walk-away settlement with mutual releases and of a defense verdict. Related definitional gap: "resolution amount" is defined as "the total amount paid or payable by Pinnacle to NovaTech." If Pinnacle prevails on a counterclaim and NovaTech pays Pinnacle, the definition yields $0 rather than a negative number, so Pinnacle would owe the full $1,420,000 in the scenario where it wins outright and collects. The letter does not address this. Also note §10 is expressly excluded from the litigation budget (§8 carve-out (c) and Exhibit B note (c)), so the $2,400,000 figure never reflects it, and the letter's only nod to independent review of the arrangement is the generic §20(b) acknowledgment that the Client "has had the opportunity to consult with independent counsel regarding these terms." ===================================================== 5. OPERATIONAL SILENCES — VERIFIED REAL, NOT ASSUMED ===================================================== I searched specifically for each of these rather than inferring from absence of memory. INVOICE FORMAT — silent. No reference to LEDES, to UTBMS task or activity codes, to any e-billing platform, or to any required invoice template. The only text is in §5: "The Firm will submit invoices electronically to the billing contact designated by the Client." §5 does specify minimum invoice content — description of services, timekeeper identity, hours, applicable rate, and a summary of disbursements — but nothing about format, structure, or delivery channel beyond "electronically." CLIENT DESIGNATED CONTACT — no clause naming or requiring one. The letter is addressed to Margaret Yeun, General Counsel. §1 references discussions with "Thomas Ridley, Associate General Counsel (Litigation)." §5 refers to "the billing contact designated by the Client" without naming anyone or requiring designation. The only contacts the letter actually fixes are firm-side: §2 designates Morrow as "the primary point of contact for day-to-day case management, strategy, and communications with the Client" and Alcott as "the relationship partner and billing partner." Morrow's October 3 email adds that "James will be your day-to-day billing contact" — again firm-side. STATUS REPORTING — silent except for one item. The only reporting obligation anywhere in the letter is §8: "The Firm shall provide quarterly budget updates to the Client summarizing actual fees incurred to date and any material changes to the projected budget for remaining phases," repeated in Exhibit B. There is no case status report requirement of any frequency, no early case assessment deliverable, no written litigation plan, no obligation to report significant developments, no obligation to give advance notice of a budget overrun (material changes are merely summarized in the next quarterly update, after the fact), and no requirement to seek approval before exceeding a phase estimate. Additional silences you will likely want in the same catalogue, all verified absent: - Billing increments — no minimum-increment requirement, nothing prohibiting block billing, nothing on quarter-hour versus tenth-hour. - No-charge categories — nothing designating any task as non-billable overhead. Notably, §2 assigns "billing review" to Alcott as a relationship-partner function, and nothing says his billing-review time is unbillable, so on the face of the letter it is chargeable at $975/hr. - Travel time — §6 governs travel expenses but the letter never says whether time spent travelling is billable, or at what rate or fraction. - Disbursement markups — §6 entitles the Firm to reimbursement for expenses without any at-cost or no-markup language. The only "at actual cost" language is confined to travel. Copying, printing, and legal research database charges are listed as reimbursable with no rate discipline. - Vendor approval — no requirement to obtain client consent before retaining third-party vendors generally. §6's $15,000 per-item prior-approval threshold and §7's e-discovery pass-through sit in unresolved tension: §7 commits the engagement to roughly $380,000 of CrossPoint services without stating whether the §6 approval gate applies. You should flag that ambiguity directly. - Data security, confidentiality of PHI, and HIPAA — the letter has a general confidentiality clause (§16) but imposes no information-security requirements, no breach-notification obligation, and no HIPAA or business-associate terms, on a healthcare client whose underlying dispute expressly involves "data integrity failures that compromised patient record accuracy" (§1). - Audit rights — none. No right to audit invoices, no fee examiner provision, no records-retention or inspection right. - Also absent: any diversity or staffing-composition reporting, any timekeeper rate freeze, any discount, any restriction on adding timekeepers or on training time for new team members, and any obligation to seek approval before substituting staff — the latter affirmatively displaced by §2's grant of "sole discretion over all staffing decisions." ===================================================== 6. HB&C / CROSSPOINT COMMERCIAL RELATIONSHIP — NOTHING IN MY FILE ===================================================== Nothing. I searched both emails for CrossPoint, vendor, e-discovery, discovery, referral, rebate, revenue, discount, and commission. Zero hits on every term — the conflicts correspondence does not discuss e-discovery or vendors at all. There is no prior disclosure of any financial interest, referral arrangement, rebate, volume discount, or revenue share anywhere in my materials. So the complete universe of disclosure available to Pinnacle, on my file, is the two phrases in §7: CrossPoint is "a strategic partner of the Firm," and it "will provide services at preferred rates available through its partnership with the Firm." I would put the point to you this way, because I think it is sharper than a bare "no disclosure" finding: §7 does not fail to disclose a relationship. It affirmatively discloses that a commercial partnership exists, and then discloses nothing whatsoever about its economics. The letter tells the client there is an arrangement, invites the client to rely on the firm's recommendation of its partner, and never says whether the firm receives anything. "Preferred rates available through its partnership with the Firm" is language that would read identically whether the preference is a pure client benefit or a shared margin. Stacked with what you already identified — sole staffing discretion under §2, a $380,000 pass-through sitting outside a budget that is expressly not a cap, no competitive bid, no client approval gate that clearly attaches, and §19 foreclosing reliance on anything said outside the four corners — the structural point is that the letter creates the referral without creating any mechanism by which Pinnacle could ever learn what it costs the firm to make it. The natural remediation ask is a written disclosure of any direct or indirect financial interest, plus either competitive bidding or a client right to select the vendor. Whether HB&C in fact receives consideration from CrossPoint is a factual question my file cannot answer, and I would not have the memo assert or imply that it does. ===================================================== That is the end of my file. Three documents, nothing after October 4, 2025, no Pinnacle-outbound correspondence. Anything further I could tell you would be inference rather than record, and I would rather you write around a clean gap than around my guesswork. Say the word if you want the raw undecoded .eml bytes, the confidentiality footer, or any other section of the letter verbatim. — Sam

Morgan — good. Nothing further needed from my side either, but one cross-link before you close, because your second vendor finding intersects with something in my file and I think it makes your point larger than you may have written it. I cannot verify your arithmetic — the CrossPoint proposal and staffing plan are not in my materials, so the volumes, seat counts, and review-rate assumptions are yours and I am taking them as given rather than confirming them. With that caveat: If contract attorney hours are understated by two to ten times, the two silences I reported in §2 stop being drafting slips and become the mechanism. The engagement letter says only that the Firm "may, from time to time, utilize contract attorneys for document review and other tasks at rates up to $350 per hour." There is nothing on whether that time is passed through at cost or billed with a markup, nothing requiring contract attorneys to be identified on invoices, and nothing requiring notice before they are added. Combine that with §2's grant of sole staffing discretion and §8's express statement that the budget is not a cap, and there is no provision anywhere in the letter that would surface the overrun to Pinnacle before it appeared on an invoice — and §5 permits invoices to arrive up to sixty days after month-end. On scale: at the $350 ceiling, the gap between the staffing plan's 750–1,000 hours and your 7,000–10,000 first-pass figure is on the order of $2.1M to $3.2M. Even your aggressive-TAR floor of 1,400–2,000 hours leaves a material gap. The upper end approaches or exceeds the entire $2,400,000 litigation budget, from a line item the staffing plan allocates $262,500–$350,000. That is the same order of magnitude as the matter's total budgeted fees, and it sits outside every control in the letter. The related item worth pairing with it: I flagged earlier that the staffing plan attributes contract attorney billing to "standard billing practices" in the engagement letter, and that no such term exists — the letter's only contract attorney provision is the $350 rate ceiling. If your exposure estimate is right, that phantom attribution is doing real work. The client is being pointed to engagement letter terms that would govern the largest uncontrolled cost in the package, and those terms are not there. That is a disclosure gap rather than a citation error, and it may deserve to sit with your contract attorney finding rather than as a separate drafting note. Your instinct to write it as a question is right, and I would keep it that way — the hours estimate depends on assumptions about culling and review rates that only HB&C and CrossPoint can supply. But the remediation ask is narrower than the uncertainty: a not-to-exceed on contract attorney hours, pass-through at cost with no markup, timekeeper-level identification on invoices, and advance notice before contract attorneys are added. Those are worth asking for regardless of whose volume estimate turns out to be correct. Use it or not as it fits what you have already filed. Nice work on the reframe. — Sam

Ten issues requiring resolution before execution', 2) TBL( ['#', 'Issue', 'OCG provision', 'Severity'], [ ['1', 'OCG never referenced in the engagement letter; §19 integration clause arguably displaces it', '§§1.1, 2.1(h)', 'CRITICAL'], ['2', 'Undisclosed and unresolved conflict — HB&C represents MedBridge, an 8% equity holder in adverse party NovaTech; no GC consent', '§2.2', 'CRITICAL'], ['3', 'Prohibited advance/blanket conflicts waiver in EL §11, with no notice or consent obligation', '§2.2', 'CRITICAL'], ['4', 'Malpractice liability capped at the lesser of $1M or fees paid (EL §13); client indemnifies Firm for its own negligence (EL §14)', '§2.3; prof. resp.', 'CRITICAL'], ['5', 'Professional liability insurance of $10M/$20M represented — below the mandatory $25M/$50M minimum', '§2.3', 'CRITICAL'], ['6', 'Success fee of up to $1,420,000 embedded in the engagement letter, uncapped, payable on dismissal', '§9.2', 'CRITICAL'], ['7', 'Every proposed rate exceeds the applicable cap; automatic recurring 5% escalation with no notice or approval', '§§3.1, 3.2', 'HIGH'], ['8', '$250,000 non-refundable retainer into the Firm\'s operating account; 15% termination fee on client-initiated termination', '§§3.6, 8.1', 'HIGH'], ['9', 'Retaining lien asserted; work product becomes client property only upon full payment', '§§7.1, 7.2', 'HIGH'], ['10', '$380,000 sole-sourced e-discovery engagement with the Firm\'s undisclosed-economics "strategic partner," outside a budget that is not a cap', '§§1.2, 4.1', 'HIGH'], ], widths=[0.32, 3.55, 1.05, 0.78], fontsize=8.5) H('C. How to read this memorandum', 2) RT([('Sections III through XIII analyse substantive issues by subject matter. Section XIV catalogues ' 'operational OCG requirements on which the engagement letter is simply silent. Section XV lists ' 'internal inconsistencies and diligence items. Section XVI consolidates the financial exposure. ' 'Section XVII sets out prioritised recommendations in the form of specific drafting asks, and ' 'Section XVIII lists directed factual questions that must be answered before execution. Appendix A ' 'is a clause-by-clause OCG compliance matrix.', {})], align='j') RT([('An important sourcing limitation applies throughout and is set out in full in Section II.B: ', {'b': True}), ('the engagement letter itself was not among the materials staged for this review. Its terms are ' 'reported here as transmitted by the matter communications analyst, in verbatim quotation where so ' 'indicated. Those quotations should be verified against the underlying document before this memorandum ' 'is used in negotiation or relied upon for any adverse action.', {})], align='j') doc.save('/tmp/memo_part.docx') print('PART 1 OK — paragraphs:', len(doc.paragraphs))

content # ===================================================================== # II. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED / SOURCES # ===================================================================== H('II. Documents Reviewed, Sources, and Limitations') H('A. Documents staged for review', 2) TBL(['Document', 'Date', 'Author / source'], [ ['Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc. Outside Counsel Guidelines (January 2024 Revision)', 'Eff. Jan. 1, 2024', 'Pinnacle — Margaret Yeun, GC'], ['Proposed Staffing Plan — NovaTech Solutions, LLC v. Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc.', 'Oct. 6, 2025', 'HB&C — Sandra K. Morrow'], ['Proposal for E-Discovery Services', 'Oct. 5, 2025', 'CrossPoint Analytics — Nathan Collier'], ], widths=[3.9, 1.05, 1.75], fontsize=9) H('B. The engagement letter was not staged — sourcing and its limits', 2) RT([('The assignment was to review "the attached proposed engagement letter and supporting documents." ', {}), ('No engagement letter was among the staged materials.', {'b': True}), (' The staffing plan references an "Engagement Letter between Hawthorne, Bellamy & Cross LLP and ' 'Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc. dated October 6, 2025" at least six times and attributes to it the ' 'terms most likely to conflict with the Guidelines — a rate escalation provision, a blended rate, the ' '$2,400,000 budget, and contract attorney billing.', {})], align='j') RT([('The letter and the related conflicts correspondence were obtained from the matter communications ' 'analyst holding the correspondence file. That file contains three documents: the unexecuted October 6, ' '2025 engagement letter (twenty sections plus Exhibit A, Rate Schedule, and Exhibit B, Preliminary ' 'Litigation Budget) and two conflicts emails. Quotations in this memorandum marked as verbatim were ' 'transmitted as verbatim; other engagement letter terms are reported as summarised.', {})], align='j') RT([('Limitation. ', {'b': True}), ('This reviewer has not personally inspected the engagement letter, its exhibits, or the native email ' 'files. Every engagement letter reference in this memorandum is second-hand. Before this memorandum is ' 'used in negotiation with HB&C, or relied upon for any adverse action, ', {}), ('the engagement letter and both exhibits should be obtained and the quotations verified.', {'b': True}), (' A single mischaracterised term would be found immediately by opposing drafting counsel and would ' 'undercut the credibility of the remaining findings.', {})], align='j') RT([('One provenance point bears noting for evidentiary purposes. The October 4, 2025 Alcott email is a ' 'normal message carrying true RFC-822 headers. The October 3, 2025 Morrow email is not: it carries a ' 'bare MIME preamble with its Date, From, To, Cc and Subject fields appearing inside the message body, ' 'which is characteristic of a message reconstructed into a file rather than exported natively from a ' 'mail system. Nothing suggests the content is unreliable, but if the Morrow email is to be used as an ' 'exhibit or relied on as a business record, the original should be pulled from Pinnacle\'s mail system.', {})], align='j') H('C. Execution status — the governing assumption', 2) RT([('This memorandum is written as a ', {}), ('pre-execution review of a proposed engagement', {'b': True}), (', which is what the documents on their face are. The staged engagement letter is unexecuted: both ' 'signature blocks are blank, the fee-election checkbox is unmarked, and the closing paragraph requests ' 'return of an executed counterpart "no later than October 18, 2025." The October 3 and October 4 ' 'correspondence corroborates a pre-execution posture.', {})], align='j') RT([('That assumption has a defined limit, and the limit matters. ', {'b': True}), ('The correspondence file ends on October 4, 2025. There is no executed counterpart, no countersignature, ' 'no post-execution billing correspondence, no amendment, and nothing at all from the intervening ' 'eleven months. Non-execution is therefore confirmed only through October 4, 2025. The absence of later ' 'correspondence is not affirmative evidence that the letter was never signed; it may simply mean that ' 'later correspondence was not staged. File metadata on the letter is a generic authoring-tool ' 'placeholder and is not probative.', {})], align='j') RT([('Execution status should be confirmed with the General Counsel or Associate General Counsel before ' 'this memorandum is relied upon.', {'b': True}), (' If the letter was in fact executed in October 2025, several recommendations change character rather ' 'than merely lapsing:', {})], align='j') BR([('the automatic 5% escalation would have taken effect on January 1, 2026 without notice, and a second ' 'would be pending for January 1, 2027 under the same no-notice mechanism;', {})]) BR([('the OCG\'s November 1 rate-change submission deadline and 30-day initial budget deadline would have ' 'run in 2025;', {})]) BR([('roughly eleven months of fees would already have been billed, converting the budget-reporting and ' 'invoice-timing points from drafting issues into retrospective compliance and recoupment questions;', {})]) BR([('the fee election under EL §3.2 would be locked, the election having been required at signing; and', {})]) BR([('the CrossPoint proposal expired by its own terms on December 4, 2025, so e-discovery would either be ' 'running on superseded pricing or have been re-quoted on terms nobody has reviewed.', {})]) RT([('Sections XVII and XVIII flag which items require retrospective treatment in that event.', {})], align='j') # ===================================================================== # III. THRESHOLD STRUCTURAL ISSUE # ===================================================================== H('III. Threshold Issue — The Guidelines Are Not Incorporated Into the Engagement Letter') RT([('Severity: CRITICAL. ', {'b': True, 'color': RED}), ('This should be resolved before any other term is negotiated, because it determines whether the ' 'remaining analysis has contractual force.', {})], align='j') H('A. What the Guidelines assume', 2) QUOTE('"The OCG are incorporated by reference into every engagement letter executed between Pinnacle and ' 'outside counsel, and they supersede any conflicting terms in engagement letters, fee agreements, ' 'retainer arrangements, or firm billing policies."', '— OCG §1.1') QUOTE('"The engagement letter must expressly reference and incorporate these Outside Counsel Guidelines. ' 'Any terms in an engagement letter that conflict with, are inconsistent with, or purport to modify ' 'these Guidelines are void and of no effect unless expressly waived in writing by the General Counsel ' 'in a separate document."', '— OCG §2.1') RT([('OCG §2.1(h) further requires that every engagement letter contain "[a]n express statement that ' 'outside counsel agrees to comply with these Guidelines in their entirety."', {})], align='j') H('B. What the engagement letter actually does', 2) RT([('The engagement letter does not reference the Outside Counsel Guidelines anywhere. ', {'b': True}), ('A case-insensitive search for "outside counsel," "guideline," "OCG," and related terms returned zero ' 'occurrences across the full body text of §§1–20, Exhibit A, Exhibit B, the document header and footer, ' 'the raw document XML, and the document package (no comments, footnotes, endnotes, tracked changes, or ' 'embedded objects). Neither conflicts email mentions them either.', {})], align='j') RT([('The same search was run against the two documents staged for this review. ', {}), ('The staffing plan and the CrossPoint proposal likewise contain no reference to the Guidelines, to any ' 'client billing policy, or to any engagement policy by any name.', {'b': True}), (' Across the entire HB&C-side package — engagement letter, exhibits, staffing plan, vendor proposal, ' 'and both conflicts emails — the Guidelines appear nowhere.', {})], align='j') RT([('The letter then closes with a full integration clause:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"This engagement letter, together with its Exhibits, constitutes the entire agreement between the ' 'Firm and the Client with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and ' 'contemporaneous agreements, representations, and understandings, whether written or oral, relating ' 'to the Firm\'s engagement by the Client in connection with the NovaTech litigation. No ' 'representations, warranties, or commitments have been made by either party except as expressly set ' 'forth herein. This engagement letter may not be amended or modified except by a written instrument ' 'signed by both parties hereto."', '— EL §19 (verbatim)') H('C. Why this is the memorandum\'s most important finding', 2) RT([('The Guidelines assert their own incorporation and primacy. But a document can only assert that of ' 'itself. The Guidelines are Pinnacle\'s unilateral statement of policy; they bind HB&C only if HB&C ' 'agrees to them. The operative contract HB&C drafted is silent about them and closes by declaring ' 'itself the entire agreement. If Pinnacle signs as drafted, HB&C has a straightforward argument that ' '§19 makes the letter the whole of the bargain and that the Guidelines — never referenced, never ' 'attached, never acknowledged in writing by the Firm — sit outside it.', {})], align='j') RT([('The second sentence of §19 deserves separate attention. ', {'b': True}), ('"No representations, warranties, or commitments have been made by either party except as expressly ' 'set forth herein" does independent work. On its face it disclaims Morrow\'s October 3 representations ' 'that the MedBridge stake is passive and that there is "no overlapping confidential information ' 'between the two engagements." It also disclaims her commitment to deliver "a confirmation from our ' 'conflicts team so you have something formal for your files." Signing the letter would have Pinnacle ' 'affirm that those representations were never made — which is precisely the disclosure Pinnacle would ' 'otherwise rely on.', {})], align='j') RT([('Every other finding in this memorandum — rate caps, the retainer, the success fee, the lien, the ' 'liability cap — is framed as a conflict between the letter and the Guidelines. Each of those framings ' 'presupposes that the Guidelines apply. Resolve incorporation and Pinnacle holds the contractual ' 'position that the conflicting terms are "void and of no effect" under OCG §2.1. Leave it unresolved ' 'and each becomes a term Pinnacle must negotiate out one at a time, from a materially weaker position.', {})], align='j') H('D. An unresolved antecedent question', 2) RT([('There is no record that the Guidelines were ever transmitted to HB&C. There is no transmittal email, ' 'no acknowledgment, no signed OCG acknowledgment page (the Guidelines carry one at the back), and no ' 'reference to the Guidelines in any HB&C communication in the correspondence file.', {})], align='j') RT([('That absence is weak evidence and should not be reported as more. ', {'b': True}), ('The correspondence file runs in one direction only — HB&C to Pinnacle. It holds no Pinnacle-outbound ' 'correspondence at all: nothing from Mr. Ridley, nothing from Ms. Yeun, no transmittal of engagement ' 'materials, no RFP or panel-admission correspondence. An OCG transmittal would almost certainly have ' 'been Pinnacle-outbound, so that file is close to the worst available place to look for it. The correct ' 'inference is that transmittal cannot be confirmed, not that it did not occur.', {})], align='j') RT([('This is resolvable internally and quickly, and it should be, because it changes the posture of the ' 'negotiation. If HB&C received the Guidelines with an RFP or on panel admission and drafted around ' 'them, that is a very different conversation from one in which the Firm never received them. The ' 'places to look are Pinnacle\'s own sent mail, the vendor-onboarding or panel-counsel file, and ' 'whoever ran the selection process that produced the October 1, 2025 call referenced in Ms. Morrow\'s ' 'email. See Section XVIII, Question 1.', {})], align='j') RT([('One indirect data point exists, and it is suggestive of posture rather than proof of anything. ' 'Ms. Morrow wrote on October 3 that "as is standard for our firm, the engagement letter will include ' 'our customary provision regarding representation of other clients in unrelated matters." That is a ' 'firm proceeding from its own form. A firm that had received the Guidelines and chosen to draft around ' 'them would sound identical.', {})], align='j') RT([('A caution on how to state this externally: it should be said that the Guidelines appear nowhere in ' 'the written record available, not that they were never raised. Ms. Morrow references a call with ' 'Mr. Ridley on Wednesday, October 1, and Mr. Alcott offers to "coordinate directly with Margaret ' 'Yeun\'s office." There is no record of what was said on any call. Oral transmittal would not survive ' '§19 in any event.', {})], align='j')

content # ===================================================================== # IV. CONFLICTS # ===================================================================== H('IV. Conflicts of Interest — The MedBridge Therapeutics Relationship') RT([('Severity: CRITICAL. ', {'b': True, 'color': RED}), ('This issue is independent of the drafting points in the remainder of this memorandum. It is not cured ' 'by redlining. It requires either a complete formal clearance and a specific informed written consent ' 'executed by the General Counsel, or the selection of different counsel.', {})], align='j') H('A. The disclosure', 2) RT([('On Friday, October 3, 2025, lead engagement partner Sandra K. Morrow wrote to Thomas Ridley, ' 'Associate General Counsel — Litigation, copying James Alcott, under the subject line "NovaTech ' 'Defense Engagement — Disclosure Regarding MedBridge Therapeutics." The material passage reads:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"Our firm currently represents MedBridge Therapeutics in a reimbursement dispute against BlueLine ' 'Insurance. It\'s a straightforward coverage matter — entirely different subject matter, different ' 'parties, and different legal issues from the NovaTech breach-of-contract litigation. No overlap ' 'whatsoever. In the course of running conflicts, we identified that MedBridge is a minority investor ' 'in NovaTech Solutions, LLC, holding approximately 8% equity. From what we understand, this is a ' 'passive financial investment — MedBridge has no seat on NovaTech\'s board and no involvement in ' 'NovaTech\'s operations or litigation decisions."', '— Morrow to Ridley, Oct. 3, 2025 (verbatim)') QUOTE('"I don\'t believe this creates a conflict of interest. ... Our work for MedBridge will in no way ' 'affect our ability to zealously defend Pinnacle\'s interests against NovaTech. That said, I\'ve ' 'asked James to follow up with a confirmation from our conflicts team so you have something formal ' 'for your files."', '— Morrow to Ridley, Oct. 3, 2025 (verbatim)') RT([('Three textual features of that disclosure are worth marking. ', {'b': True}), ('First, "From what we understand" qualifies the passivity assertion — the Firm is relaying its ' 'understanding, not a verified fact, and the memorandum should not treat MedBridge\'s passivity as ' 'established. Second, the conclusion "I don\'t believe this creates a conflict of interest" is the ' 'engaged partner\'s own assessment, delivered before and in place of the conflicts team\'s. Third, the ' 'email pre-announces that the letter "will include our customary provision regarding representation of ' 'other clients in unrelated matters" — advance notice that the Firm intended to paper the conflict ' 'through a form advance waiver rather than a specific consent.', {})], align='j') RT([('To Ms. Morrow\'s credit, the disclosure was volunteered, prompt, and specific as to the equity ' 'percentage. The difficulty is not that the relationship was concealed. It is what happened next.', {})], align='j') H('B. The promised clearance', 2) RT([('The follow-up arrived the next morning, Saturday, October 4, 2025, from Mr. Alcott to Mr. Ridley, ' 'copying Ms. Morrow, under the subject line "RE: Conflicts Clearance." It is expressly framed as the ' 'response to the MedBridge disclosure:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"Sandra pinged me yesterday regarding the MedBridge Therapeutics matter and asked that I circle back ' 'with you directly to confirm where we landed on conflicts.\n\n' 'We\'ve completed our standard conflicts check across all four offices — Washington, Charlotte, ' 'Atlanta, and New York — in connection with the proposed engagement to defend Pinnacle Health ' 'Systems, Inc. in NovaTech Solutions, LLC v. Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc., Case No. ' '3:25-cv-01847-MRD (W.D.N.C.). The review was run against NovaTech Solutions, LLC, its known ' 'principals, and opposing counsel Prescott Lane LLP. We see no issues that would preclude our ' 'representation of Pinnacle in this matter."', '— Alcott to Ridley, Oct. 4, 2025 (verbatim)') RT([('The problem is precise, and it should be stated precisely. ', {'b': True}), ('The email names MedBridge in its second sentence and is expressly presented as responsive to the ' 'MedBridge disclosure. It then describes a conflicts search whose stated scope was run against ' '"NovaTech Solutions, LLC, its known principals, and opposing counsel Prescott Lane LLP" — a scope ' 'that does not include MedBridge, MedBridge\'s own matters, or NovaTech\'s equity holders. It returns ' 'an unqualified conclusion, "no issues that would preclude our representation," without ever ' 'analysing, or even restating, the 8% equity relationship that prompted it.', {})], align='j') RT([('So the document presents as responsive to the disclosure while not performing the analysis the ' 'disclosure called for. ', {'b': True}), ('A reader encountering "RE: Conflicts Clearance" in the file without the prior day\'s email would take ' 'away an unqualified clearance. That is the practical risk: the file now contains a clean clearance ' 'that does not address the one issue it was created to address.', {})], align='j') RT([('Two further gaps. Ms. Morrow promised "a confirmation from our conflicts team." What was delivered is ' 'a partner\'s email reporting that a check was run — not a memorandum from the conflicts function, not ' 'signed by anyone in it, and not a conflicts clearance letter of the kind OCG §2.2 requires. And the ' 'clearance was delivered to Mr. Ridley; as set out below, the consent the Guidelines require must come ' 'from the General Counsel.', {})], align='j') H('C. The engagement letter contradicts the disclosure', 2) RT([('EL §11 is two paragraphs. The first reads, verbatim:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"The Firm has conducted a conflicts check and has determined that it has no current conflicts of ' 'interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this engagement. The Firm is committed to ' 'maintaining the highest standards of professional responsibility and will monitor for potential ' 'conflicts on an ongoing basis."', '— EL §11, ¶1 (verbatim)') RT([('Section 11 contains no disclosure of the MedBridge representation, no disclosure of the 8% NovaTech ' 'equity stake, no reference to the October 3 or October 4 emails, and no carve-out preserving them. ' 'Read with §19, that omission is the point worth pressing: ', {}), ('the disclosure lives only in pre-contractual emails that the integration clause purports to supersede.', {'b': True}), (' If Pinnacle executes the letter, it executes a representation that is in tension with what the Firm ' 'told it eight weeks earlier, in a document that simultaneously disclaims the earlier telling.', {})], align='j') H('D. The advance waiver', 2) RT([('The second paragraph of §11 reads, verbatim:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"The Client acknowledges and agrees that the Firm represents, and may in the future represent, other ' 'clients whose interests may be adverse to the Client in matters unrelated to this engagement, ' 'including in matters involving other healthcare companies, healthcare litigation, and related ' 'regulatory matters. The Client hereby consents to such representations and waives any conflict of ' 'interest arising therefrom, provided that the Firm shall not represent any party directly adverse to ' 'the Client in the specific NovaTech litigation that is the subject of this engagement. The Firm shall ' 'not be required to provide notice to or obtain consent from the Client before undertaking any such ' 'unrelated adverse representation. This advance waiver is intended to permit the Firm to continue to ' 'serve its diverse client base without restriction, consistent with applicable rules of professional ' 'conduct."', '— EL §11, ¶2 (verbatim)') RT([('This is precisely what OCG §2.2 forbids, in terms:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"Blanket or advance waivers of future conflicts are not acceptable. Any waiver of a specific, ' 'identified conflict must be set forth in a separate written consent executed by the General Counsel ' 'after full disclosure of all material facts. Outside counsel may not rely on a general waiver ' 'provision in an engagement letter to satisfy its conflict-of-interest disclosure obligations."', '— OCG §2.2') RT([('Three defects, in ascending order of seriousness. ', {'b': True}), ('(i) It is a blanket advance waiver in an engagement letter, which the Guidelines do not accept in any ' 'form. (ii) It affirmatively disclaims any obligation to give notice — so Pinnacle would not learn of ' 'future adverse representations at all, which forecloses even the ability to object. (iii) Most ' 'seriously, it is drafted to sweep in a conflict the Firm had already identified and disclosed. An ' 'advance waiver of ', {}), ('unknown future', {'i': True}), (' conflicts obtained from a sophisticated client can be valid; a general waiver cannot launder a ' 'specific, known, undisclosed conflict. Whatever §11 ¶2 does, it cannot supply informed consent to the ' 'MedBridge relationship, because §11 ¶1 represents that no such relationship exists.', {})], align='j') RT([('Note also the carve-out\'s narrowness: the Firm agrees only not to represent a party "directly adverse ' 'to the Client in the specific NovaTech litigation." That does not prevent the Firm from taking on ' 'NovaTech itself, or MedBridge, in any other matter, at any time, without telling Pinnacle.', {})], align='j') H('E. Application of OCG §2.2 — the Guidelines resolve this on their own terms', 2) RT([('The Guidelines do not require a judgment call here. They define the trigger numerically and then ' 'state the consequence.', {})], align='j') TBL(['OCG requirement', 'Text', 'Status'], [ ['Disclose representations of entities with a material financial interest in an adverse party', '§2.2(b): "material financial interest" defined as "a 5% or greater equity stake"', 'TRIGGERED — 8% > 5%'], ['Prohibition on accepting the engagement', '§2.2: "shall not accept any engagement ... if the firm concurrently represents ... any entity ' 'holding a material financial interest in such adverse party, unless a detailed written disclosure ' 'is provided and informed written consent is obtained from the General Counsel"', 'NOT SATISFIED'], ['Written conflicts clearance letter addressing §2.2(a)–(d)', '§2.2: required before commencing any work', 'NOT DELIVERED — two emails only'], ['Informed written consent from the General Counsel', '§2.2; §1.3 ("Waivers ... must be in writing and signed by the General Counsel")', 'NOT OBTAINED — sent to AGC'], ['No blanket or advance waivers', '§2.2', 'VIOLATED — EL §11 ¶2'], ['Conflicts check complete before any work', '§2.2; §2.1 (no substantive work before full execution)', 'VIOLATED — see §IV.G'], ], widths=[1.75, 3.05, 1.7], fontsize=8.5) RT([('The addressee point is not a technicality. ', {'b': True}), ('OCG §2.2 permits the clearance ', {}), ('letter', {'i': True}), (' to go to "Pinnacle\'s General Counsel or her designee," but the consent that lifts the prohibition ' 'on accepting the engagement must be "obtained from the General Counsel," and OCG §1.3 requires that ' 'waivers be "in writing and signed by the General Counsel." Both emails went to Mr. Ridley. Absent an ' 'express designation, Mr. Ridley cannot supply the consent, and nothing in the record suggests he ' 'purported to. Mr. Alcott in fact offered to "coordinate directly with Margaret Yeun\'s office"; there ' 'is no record that he did.', {})], align='j') H('F. The substantive conflict is real, and more concrete than "passive investor"', 2) RT([('Even setting the Guidelines aside, the Firm\'s "no overlap whatsoever" framing understates the ' 'problem. HB&C does not represent NovaTech, so this is not direct adversity in the classic sense. The ' 'live question is the material-limitation prong: whether there is a significant risk that the ' 'representation of Pinnacle will be materially limited by the Firm\'s responsibilities to MedBridge. ' 'Three matter-specific points suggest it is.', {})], align='j') RT([('First, the economics are not trivial. ', {'b': True}), ('An 8% stake in a $14.2 million claim is roughly $1.14 million of value to MedBridge if NovaTech ' 'prevails. A vigorous defence — and any counterclaim — directly reduces the value of HB&C\'s other ' 'client\'s investment. The interest is indirect but it is neither remote nor abstract.', {})], align='j') RT([('Second, and not addressed anywhere in the record: ', {'b': True}), ('MedBridge is a likely third-party discovery target in this very case.', {'b': True}), (' Pinnacle\'s defence rests on termination for cause under MSA §12.2, grounded in persistent outages, ' 'unresolved software defects, and data integrity failures. As a NovaTech equity holder, MedBridge may ' 'well hold investor updates, board or observer materials, diligence files, and internal assessments of ' 'NovaTech\'s platform stability and of the Pinnacle implementation specifically — which is close to ' 'ideal evidence for the material-breach defence, generated outside NovaTech\'s litigation posture. ' 'HB&C\'s duties of loyalty and confidentiality to MedBridge would materially limit its willingness and ' 'its ability to pursue that discovery, to subpoena MedBridge, to depose its personnel, or to use what ' 'it finds. That converts "passive investor, no conflict" into a concrete, matter-specific limitation ' 'on the defence Pinnacle is buying.', {})], align='j') RT([('Third, the Firm has not disclosed what it knows. ', {'b': True}), ('The record does not say whether HB&C advised MedBridge on the NovaTech investment, whether it holds ' 'MedBridge confidential information bearing on NovaTech, or whether any lawyer who worked on MedBridge ' 'matters would touch this one. Ms. Morrow\'s assertion that there is "no overlapping confidential ' 'information" is unsupported and, under EL §19, disclaimed. The relationship is imputed across the ' 'Firm in any event.', {})], align='j') H('G. Work commenced before execution and before clearance', 2) RT([('Both emails describe substantive work already underway. Ms. Morrow: "we\'re already doing preliminary ' 'research on Pinnacle\'s termination-for-cause defense so we can hit the ground running once the ' 'engagement is executed." Mr. Alcott: Priya Dasgupta, Kevin Marsh and Rita Solano "are already ' 'reserved and ready to ramp up."', {})], align='j') RT([('Research on the core defence theory is substantive work. OCG §2.1 requires that engagements be ' 'memorialised in a written engagement letter "before any substantive work commences" and that counsel ' '"not commence substantive work on a matter until the engagement letter has been fully executed by ' 'both parties." OCG §2.2 requires the conflicts check to be complete "[b]efore commencing any work." ' 'On this record, work began before execution and while the MedBridge question was open.', {})], align='j') RT([('Practical consequence: Pinnacle should state in writing that no pre-execution time will be paid, and ' 'require the Firm to confirm that no pre-engagement time has been or will be recorded to the matter. ' 'The amount is unknown and should be ascertained.', {})], align='j') H('H. What must happen before this engagement can proceed', 2) BR([('A complete, formal conflicts clearance letter', {'b': True}), (' meeting OCG §2.2(a)–(d), signed, covering all four offices, and expressly addressing MedBridge, ' 'MedBridge\'s own matters, and NovaTech\'s equity holders. content # ===================================================================== # VII. BUDGET # ===================================================================== H('VII. Budget and Cost Management') H('A. "The budget is an estimate only and is not a cap on fees"', 2) RT([('That sentence appears in EL §8 and is repeated in Exhibit B. It reverses the Guidelines\' allocation ' 'of overrun risk. OCG §4.3 provides that Pinnacle "will not pay fees or costs that exceed the approved ' 'budget unless prior written approval has been obtained," and that "[o]utside counsel bears the ' 'financial risk of budget overruns that are not pre-approved."', {})], align='j') RT([('The disclaimer does not stand alone. Combined with EL §2 (sole staffing discretion), EL §5 (60-day ' 'invoice submission), EL §8 (quarterly summaries only, with no overrun notice or approval gate), and ' 'four separate budget carve-outs, ', {}), ('Pinnacle would have no effective cost control mechanism at any point in the engagement.', {'b': True}), (' The Firm could add timekeepers without notice, bill at automatically escalating above-cap rates, ' 'exceed the estimate without asking, and report the result up to a quarter after the fact.', {})], align='j') H('B. The carve-outs', 2) RT([('EL §8 excludes from the $2,400,000 budget: (a) e-discovery, estimated separately at $380,000; (b) the ' '$250,000 engagement retainer; (c) the success fee, if earned; and (d) "extraordinary or unanticipated ' 'expenses."', {})], align='j') RT([('OCG §4.1 requires the opposite, in terms: the budget "must include all anticipated costs, including ' 'but not limited to attorney fees, paralegal fees, expert fees, e-discovery costs, travel expenses, ' 'court costs, filing fees, and any other disbursements. All cost categories must be reflected in the ' 'budget." It adds that counsel "should err on the side of over-inclusion." Carve-out (a) removes an ' 'expressly enumerated category. Carve-out (d) is undefined and unbounded — it is not a carve-out so ' 'much as an open door, and it should be struck or replaced with a defined dollar threshold subject to ' 'prior written approval.', {})], align='j') RT([('The consequence for the headline figure is that $2,400,000 does not describe the engagement:', {})], align='j') TBL(['Component', 'Amount', 'In the "$2.4M budget"?'], [ ['Attorney and paralegal fees (core team, at proposed rates)', '$1,141,500', 'Yes'], ['Contract attorney fees (750–1,000 hrs at up to $350)', '$262,500–$350,000', 'Yes (within Phase 1)'], ['Expert fees and costs', '$224,000', 'Yes (within Phase 2)'], ['Unitemised disbursements, contingencies, trial costs', '$684,500–$772,000', 'Yes'], ['**Stated litigation budget', '**$2,400,000', '**—'], ['E-discovery (CrossPoint)', '$380,000', 'No — carve-out (a)'], ['Engagement retainer (non-refundable, additive)', '$250,000', 'No — carve-out (b)'], ['Success fee, if earned', 'up to $1,420,000', 'No — carve-out (c)'], ['"Extraordinary or unanticipated expenses"', 'undefined', 'No — carve-out (d)'], ['**Total potential outside counsel cost', '**up to $4,450,000', '**—'], ], widths=[3.15, 1.65, 1.7], fontsize=8.5) RT([('$4,450,000 is ', {}), ('31.3% of the $14.2 million pleaded demand', {'b': True}), (', before any escalation, and under a budget that is expressly not a cap. That proportion should itself ' 'prompt a strategic conversation about early resolution, discussed at subsection D below.', {})], align='j') H('C. Budget detail, process, and missing phases', 2) RT([('The phase-level detail thins sharply after the fee tables. Reconciling the staffing plan\'s timekeeper ' 'tables against its own phase targets:', {})], align='j') TBL(['Phase', 'Target', 'Itemised fees', 'Other itemised', 'Unitemised', '% unitemised'], [ ['1 — Motions & discovery', '$1,050,000', '$532,000', '$262,500–$350,000 (contract attys)', '$168,000–$255,500', '16–24%'], ['2 — Experts', '$420,000', '$196,000', '$224,000 (experts)', '$0', '0%'], ['3 — Trial preparation', '$530,000', '$264,250', '—', '$265,750', '50.1%'], ['4 — Trial', '$400,000', '$149,250', '—', '$250,750', '62.7%'], ['**Total', '**$2,400,000', '**$1,141,500', '**$486,500–$574,000', '**$684,500–$772,000', '**29–32%'], ], widths=[1.55, 0.95, 0.95, 1.4, 1.1, 0.75], fontsize=8.5) RT([('Roughly ', {}), ('30% of the budget — some $684,500 to $772,000 — is unitemised', {'b': True}), (', described only as "pre-trial costs, courtroom technology, contingencies," "trial logistics, ' 'courtroom technology, daily transcript costs, and other trial-related disbursements." For Phases 3 ' 'and 4 the unitemised share is the majority of the phase. OCG §4.1 requires a breakdown by phase in ' 'which "[a]ll cost categories must be reflected." Phase 2, by contrast, has no contingency at all — ' '$196,000 plus $224,000 equals $420,000 exactly — which is a different kind of problem, since expert ' 'costs are among the least predictable in the matter.', {})], align='j') BR([('No ADR or settlement phase. ', {'b': True}), ('OCG §4.1(e) expressly requires a phase for "[m]ediation, settlement efforts, or other alternative ' 'dispute resolution." None of the four phases includes one, and no line item anywhere provides for ' 'mediation. On a matter where projected defence costs approach a third of the pleaded demand, this is ' 'the most conspicuous omission in the budget.', {})]) BR([('No appellate phase. That may be acceptable, but it should be an ' 'express, priced exclusion agreed by Pinnacle rather than a silent one.', {})]) BR([('Case assessment is not separately budgeted. ', {'b': True}), ('OCG §4.1(a) contemplates a discrete "[c]ase assessment and strategy development" line; it is folded ' 'into Phase 1.', {})]) BR([('No budget presentation. Nothing in the ' 'record indicates this occurred. It should be scheduled as a condition of engagement.', {})]) BR([('Reporting is quarterly and retrospective only. ', {'b': True}), ('EL §8 provides quarterly summaries. The letter has no variance trigger at all — a material overrun ' 'would simply be summarised in the next quarterly report, after the money is spent.', {})]) RT([('One scheduling observation: Phase 1 runs November 2025 to September 2026 while Phase 2 begins in July ' '2026. The three-month overlap is unremarkable in litigation but will complicate phase-level ' 'budget-to-actual reporting, and the reporting format should account for it.', {})], align='j') H('D. A proportionality observation', 2) RT([('This is a $14.2 million contract dispute in which the defence is projected to cost between $2.78 ' 'million and $4.45 million. OCG §9.1 encourages ' 'alternative fee arrangements, and this matter is a strong candidate for a phased fixed or capped fee, ' 'particularly for Phase 1, where a $1,050,000 discovery allocation is the largest single block of spend ' 'and the most susceptible to scope drift.', {})], align='j') RT([('Early mediation should be priced and calendared rather than omitted. Note the interaction with the ' 'success fee, which cuts against it: under EL §10 as drafted, the Firm is indifferent between a $7.1 ' 'million settlement and a $14 million judgment, but captures over $1.1 million if the matter resolves ' 'at $3 million. Removing §10 removes that distortion from the settlement conversation entirely.', {})], align='j') # ===================================================================== # VIII. STAFFING # ===================================================================== H('VIII. Staffing') H('A. "Sole discretion" — asserted three times across two documents', 2) RT([('EL §2 grants the Firm "sole discretion over all staffing decisions," including addition, substitution ' 'or removal of timekeepers, with no client consent or notice right. The staffing plan repeats it ' 'twice: §3 ("The Firm shall have sole discretion over all staffing decisions") and §6 ("The Firm ' 'maintains sole discretion with respect to the assignment and management of personnel on this matter, ' 'and may add, substitute, or reassign attorneys and support staff as necessary"). The staffing plan is ' 'faithfully reflecting the engagement letter; this is a consistent position rather than a drafting slip.', {})], align='j') RT([('OCG §6.2 states the contrary position in equally direct terms:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"Outside counsel does not have unilateral discretion over staffing decisions on Pinnacle matters. ' 'The firm must consult with and obtain approval from Pinnacle before materially altering the ' 'composition of the engagement team. Pinnacle\'s right to approve staffing extends to the lead ' 'partner, all other partners, all senior associates, and any specialist or of counsel attorney ' 'assigned to the matter."', '— OCG §6.2') RT([('The Guidelines require fourteen calendar days\' advance written notice for any change at senior ' 'associate level or above, identifying the timekeeper, the reason, and for additions the ' 'qualifications, rate and role, with Pinnacle reserving the right to reject. Changes below that level ' 'require contemporaneous written notice and must respect the rate caps. Fees for a timekeeper added ' 'without proper notice "may result in disallowance ... for all time billed prior to proper ' 'notification."', {})], align='j') RT([('Staffing plan §3 compounds the issue: the Firm "may supplement the team with associates from other ' 'offices (Atlanta, New York, Washington, D.C.) as workload requires," and "[a]ll supplemental attorneys ' 'and staff will be assigned at rates consistent with the Firm\'s standard rate schedule for their ' 'experience level and role." That formulation ties additions to the Firm\'s standard rates — which are ' 'already above cap — rather than to the OCG maxima. Any replacement clause must bind additions to the ' 'caps expressly.', {})], align='j') H('B. Contract attorneys', 2) RT([('EL §2 permits contract attorneys "for document review and other tasks at rates up to $350 per hour," ' 'echoed in Exhibit A and in staffing plan §3. OCG §6.3 caps document-review contract attorney rates at ' '$225 and permits up to the junior associate cap of $425 only for substantive work such as motion ' 'drafting or legal research, and then only with Pinnacle\'s prior approval. The $350 rate for document ' 'review exceeds the applicable cap by 55.6%.', {})], align='j') RT([('OCG §6.3 also requires prior written approval before any contract attorney is used, supported by the ' 'proposed scope, qualifications, rate and duration. The staffing plan instead asserts a unilateral ' 'reservation of right. And as reported, the engagement letter contains no provision addressing whether ' 'contract attorney time is passed through at cost or marked up, no identification requirement, and no ' 'staffing-notice obligation — a significant gap where 750 to 1,000 hours are contemplated, and a far ' 'larger one if the volume is what Section XI.C suggests.', {})], align='j') RT([('A drafting-attribution point worth raising with the Firm: ', {'b': True}), ('staffing plan §3 states that contract attorney "time will be billed in accordance with the standard ' 'billing practices outlined in the Engagement Letter." The engagement letter contains no such term. ' 'The only text on point is the bare rate permission in §2 and the Exhibit A line. The staffing plan ' 'attributes to the letter a billing framework the letter does not contain.', {})], align='j') H('C. Two partners, and the billing partner\'s 120 hours', 2) RT([('Mr. Alcott is allocated 120 hours at $975, totalling $117,000, for a role described as "strategic ' 'oversight, client communications, budget management, billing review, and engagement compliance," ' 'including "invoice preparation and review." He appears in all four phases, including 25 hours at ' 'trial and 40 hours in Phase 1 alongside Ms. Morrow.', {})], align='j') BR([('Much of the described role is not legal services. ', {'b': True}), ('Invoice preparation, billing review and engagement compliance are administrative functions. OCG ' '§5.4(d) makes firm overhead non-reimbursable, and it is not customary for a client to pay partner ' 'rates for the preparation of the bills it receives. As reported, nothing in the engagement letter ' 'designates any of this time as non-billable — so on the face of the letter it is chargeable at $975 ' 'an hour.', {})]) BR([('Duplicative attendance requires pre-approval. ', {'b': True}), ('OCG §6.1 provides that Pinnacle "will not pay for more than one partner attending routine ' 'depositions, hearings, or internal strategy meetings absent prior written approval," and that it will ' 'not pay for multiple attorneys at the same proceeding unless pre-approved and justified. Two equity ' 'partners across all four phases needs justification phase by phase.', {})]) BR([('The travel overlay. ', {'b': True}), ('Mr. Alcott sits in Washington, D.C. on a Charlotte matter. His attendance generates travel cost and ' 'travel time that a Charlotte-staffed team would not. OCG §5.3 requires pre-approval for all travel; ' 'and as reported the letter does not say whether travel time is billable at all, or at what fraction.', {})]) RT([('Recommendation: reduce or eliminate the billing-partner allocation; designate invoice preparation, ' 'billing review and engagement compliance as non-billable; and require pre-approval for any proceeding ' 'attended by more than one partner.', {})], align='j') H('D. Diversity', 2) RT([('OCG §6.4 requires good-faith efforts to staff matters with attorneys from diverse backgrounds and ' 'requires quarterly diversity reports to the General Counsel\'s office, in Pinnacle\'s format, within ' 'thirty days of each quarter-end. The staffing plan contains no diversity information and no ' 'acknowledgment of the reporting obligation, and the engagement letter is silent. Both should be ' 'corrected: a diversity statement accompanying the staffing plan, and the reporting commitment in the ' 'engagement letter.', {})], align='j')
