content # ===================================================================== # IX. EXPENSES / INVOICING # ===================================================================== H('IX. Expenses, Invoicing, and Payment') H('A. Expense authority is three times the permitted threshold', 2) RT([('EL §6 permits the Firm to incur individual expenses up to $15,000 per item without prior written ' 'approval. OCG §5.2 sets the threshold at $5,000 and states that it "applies to all categories of ' 'expenses without exception, including but not limited to expert witness fees, consultant fees, ' 'deposition costs, travel expenses, e-discovery processing charges, filing fees, and any other ' 'individual cost item or service." The letter grants three times the authority the Guidelines allow, ' 'across every category the Guidelines expressly enumerate.', {})], align='j') H('B. Business-class travel is specifically prohibited', 2) RT([('EL §6 permits partners to fly business class on flights over two hours. OCG §5.3 anticipates and ' 'rejects exactly this:', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"Airfare. Economy or coach class only. Pinnacle will not reimburse first-class or business-class ' 'airfare under any circumstances, regardless of the seniority of the traveling attorney or the ' 'duration of the flight."', '— OCG §5.3') RT([('The two qualifiers in the Guidelines — seniority and duration — are the two conditions EL §6 relies ' 'on. The clause is void and should be struck. In practice its bite here is limited, since Washington ' 'to Charlotte is well under two hours, but the principle should not be conceded, and OCG §5.3\'s ' 'remaining limits (standard room rates, $75 per person per day for meals, pre-approval for rental cars ' 'and for all travel) need to be incorporated.', {})], align='j') H('C. Disbursements, and the absence of at-cost discipline', 2) RT([('EL §6 entitles the Firm to reimbursement of expenses without any at-cost or no-markup language; the ' 'only "actual cost" language is confined to travel. Copying, printing and legal research database ' 'charges are treated as reimbursable with no rate discipline. OCG §5.4 makes several of these ' 'categories non-reimbursable outright:', {})], align='j') TBL(['Non-reimbursable under OCG §5.4', 'Status in the engagement letter'], [ ['(a) Overtime / after-hours secretarial and administrative charges', 'Not excluded'], ['(b) Westlaw, LexisNexis, Bloomberg and other research platform charges, absent a pre-approved ' 'discrete project', 'Expressly listed as reimbursable'], ['(c) Local travel within the metropolitan area of the handling office', 'Not excluded'], ['(d) Firm overhead, including internal copying for jobs under 500 pages', 'Copying/printing ' 'reimbursable with no threshold'], ['(e) Internal technology charges — email, file storage, IT support, standard software', 'Not excluded'], ['(f) CLE, bar dues, professional development', 'Not excluded'], ['(g) Meals other than during approved travel or approved trial working meals', 'Not excluded'], ['(h) Personal expenses', 'Not excluded'], ], widths=[4.0, 2.5], fontsize=8.5) RT([('A general no-markup provision should be added: all disbursements at actual cost, no administrative ' 'surcharge, with supporting documentation for any item above $250 as OCG §3.4(e) requires.', {})], align='j') H('D. Invoice format, timing, and interest', 2) TBL(['Requirement', 'OCG', 'Engagement letter'], [ ['Format', 'LEDES 1998B via Pinnacle\'s designated e-billing platform (§3.4)', 'Silent — "submit invoices electronically to the billing contact designated by the Client" (§5)'], ['Submission deadline', 'Within 45 days of month-end; reducible or rejectable thereafter; unpaid ' 'after 90 days absent GC approval (§3.4)', '60 days after month-end (§5)'], ['Narrative detail', 'Minimum six-word task descriptions; block billing "strictly prohibited" (§3.4(b))', 'Silent — no block-billing prohibition, no minimum increment'], ['Budget-to-actual', 'Cumulative comparison required on every invoice (§3.4(f))', 'Not required'], ['Expense documentation', 'Receipts for any item above $250 (§3.4(e))', 'Not required'], ['Payment', '30 days from receipt AND approval of a compliant invoice; right to dispute, reduce or ' 'withhold; undisputed portion paid on time (§3.5)', '30 days from invoice date (§5)'], ['Late payment', 'No interest provision', '18% per annum (§5)'], ['Suspension', 'Not permitted; withdrawal requires 60 days\' notice and Pinnacle\'s consent (§8.2)', 'Firm "reserves the right to suspend work for non-payment" (§5)'], ], widths=[1.25, 2.6, 2.65], fontsize=8.5) RT([('Two of these are more than administrative. ', {'b': True})], align='j') RT([('The interest provision interacts badly with Pinnacle\'s right to dispute. ', {'b': True}), ('Under OCG §3.5, payment runs from receipt ', {}), ('and approval', {'i': True}), (' of a ', {}), ('compliant', {'i': True}), (' invoice, and Pinnacle may withhold disputed line items while paying the undisputed balance. Under EL ' '§5, interest accrues at 18% per annum from the invoice date — including, on its face, on amounts ' 'Pinnacle is entitled to dispute and on invoices that are non-compliant in format. Given that OCG §12.2 ' 'contemplates routine adjustment of non-compliant entries and §13.1 allows sixty days to raise a ' 'billing dispute, this clause would penalise Pinnacle for exercising rights the Guidelines reserve to ' 'it.', {})], align='j') RT([('The right to suspend work is the more serious of the two. ', {'b': True}), ('A firm that stops work mid-discovery over a billing dispute exposes the client to missed deadlines, ' 'waived objections, adverse inferences and sanctions. OCG §8.2 permits no such thing: withdrawal ' 'requires sixty days\' advance written notice, Pinnacle\'s written consent, a transition plan, and ' '"maintaining full staffing, work effort, and responsiveness" throughout the notice period. The ' 'suspension right should be deleted outright, not qualified.', {})], align='j') # ===================================================================== # X. RISK ALLOCATION # ===================================================================== H('X. Risk Allocation — Insurance, Liability, Indemnity, Lien, and Forum') H('A. Professional liability insurance is below the mandatory minimum', 2) RT([('EL §12 represents professional liability coverage of "$10,000,000 per occurrence and $20,000,000 in ' 'the aggregate," maintained "or substantially equivalent coverage" for the engagement duration. OCG ' '§2.3 requires $25,000,000 per occurrence and $50,000,000 in the aggregate.', {})], align='j') TBL(['', 'OCG §2.3 minimum', 'EL §12 representation', 'Shortfall'], [ ['Per occurrence', '$25,000,000', '$10,000,000', '$15,000,000'], ['Aggregate', '$50,000,000', '$20,000,000', '$30,000,000'], ], widths=[1.3, 1.75, 1.85, 1.6], fontsize=9) RT([('This is framed by the Guidelines as a disqualifier rather than a negotiating position: "Pinnacle will ' 'not engage, and will not continue to engage, any firm whose professional liability insurance falls ' 'below these minimums." Related defects: no certificate of insurance has been provided (OCG §2.3 ' 'requires proof with the conflicts clearance letter at the outset and annually thereafter); there is no ' 'representation that the carrier is rated A- or better by A.M. Best; there is no representation that ' 'the policy lacks exclusions bearing on this engagement; there is no commitment to notify Pinnacle if ' 'coverage lapses or is reduced; and "or substantially equivalent coverage" is undefined and should not ' 'be accepted.', {})], align='j') H('B. The liability cap makes the insurance representation largely decorative', 2) RT([('EL §13 caps the Firm\'s total aggregate liability — expressly including for malpractice — at "the ' 'lesser of (a) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) or (b) the total fees actually paid by the Client."', {})], align='j') RT([('Read against §12, the effect is that the $10M/$20M coverage representation is close to meaningless: ' 'the Firm has contracted its exposure down to at most $1,000,000 regardless of what its policy would ' 'respond to. On a matter with $14.2 million at stake, involving the defence of a health system\'s ' 'termination decision and the handling of patient-data-adjacent discovery, a $1,000,000 ceiling on ' 'every conceivable claim — including negligent handling of the defence itself — is not a rational ' 'allocation of risk. The "lesser of" construction also means that early in the engagement, when fees ' 'paid are low, the cap is lower still.', {})], align='j') RT([('The enforceability of a prospective malpractice limitation is a separate and serious question, ' 'addressed at Section XIII.', {})], align='j') H('C. The client indemnifies the Firm for the Firm\'s own negligence', 2) RT([('EL §14 requires Pinnacle to indemnify the Firm against claims "arising out of or relating to the ' 'engagement or any services provided hereunder," carved back only for the Firm\'s "willful ' 'misconduct." Two consequences follow from that drafting. Negligence is indemnified, which is to say ' 'the client bears the cost of its own lawyer\'s errors. And because the carve-out is limited to wilful ' 'misconduct, ', {}), ('gross negligence and recklessness are indemnified as well', {'b': True}), ('. The provision is one-way; there is no reciprocal Firm indemnity.', {})], align='j') RT([('Functionally §14 does the same work as §13 by a different route, and it should be struck. If any ' 'indemnity is retained it should be mutual, limited to third-party claims, and carved back for the ' 'Firm\'s negligence, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, and breach of confidentiality or data ' 'security obligations.', {})], align='j') H('D. The retaining lien and the payment condition on work product', 2) RT([('EL §15 asserts a retaining lien on all files and work product until all invoices are paid in full, ' 'and provides that work product becomes Client property only "upon full payment." Both halves collide ' 'head-on with the Guidelines.', {})], align='j') QUOTE('"Outside counsel shall not assert, claim, or enforce any lien — whether retaining lien, charging ' 'lien, attorney\'s lien, or otherwise — on any files, work product, documents, correspondence, or ' 'other materials belonging to Pinnacle. All files and work product must be promptly delivered to ' 'Pinnacle upon request, regardless of whether any invoices, fees, or costs remain outstanding and ' 'regardless of whether any billing dispute is pending. ... By accepting an engagement from Pinnacle, ' 'outside counsel expressly waives any right to assert a retaining lien, charging lien, or other ' 'possessory or non-possessory lien."', '— OCG §7.2') QUOTE('"Pinnacle\'s ownership of work product is absolute and is not contingent upon payment of any ' 'outstanding fees or invoices."', '— OCG §7.1') RT([('OCG §7.2 goes further than prohibition: it provides that asserting such a lien "constitutes a material ' 'breach of these Guidelines and may result in immediate termination of the engagement, removal from ' 'Pinnacle\'s approved outside counsel list, and such other consequences as Pinnacle may deem ' 'appropriate." A clause the Guidelines treat as a material breach if invoked should not be accepted ' 'into the contract in the first place.', {})], align='j') RT([('The practical stakes are highest precisely when they matter most. Combined with §5\'s suspension ' 'right, §9\'s termination fee and §4\'s non-refundable retainer, a billing dispute during Phase 1 could ' 'leave Pinnacle unable to obtain its own file, unable to transition counsel without paying $475,000, ' 'and facing a firm entitled to stop work — while under a court schedule.', {})], align='j') H('E. Three documents, three governing laws, two incompatible forums', 2) TBL(['Document', 'Governing law', 'Forum / dispute mechanism'], [ ['Pinnacle OCG (§§13.2, 14.1)', 'North Carolina', 'Negotiation, then mediation in Charlotte, then state or federal courts in Mecklenburg County, N.C.'], ['HB&C engagement letter (§§17, 18)', 'District of Columbia', 'Mandatory binding AAA arbitration in Washington, D.C., single arbitrator, expressly covering ' 'malpractice, with jury-trial waiver; D.C. exclusive jurisdiction'], ['CrossPoint proposal (§V)', 'Virginia', 'Not specified'], ], widths=[1.85, 1.35, 3.3], fontsize=8.5) RT([('The engagement letter\'s choice is difficult to justify on the merits. This is a Western District of ' 'North Carolina case, brought against a North Carolina-headquartered client, governed by a North ' 'Carolina-law contract, defended by a Charlotte-based lead partner and a Charlotte-based team, with a ' 'North Carolina paralegal handling W.D.N.C. filings. The only D.C. connections are Mr. Alcott\'s office ' 'and the Firm\'s preference. Requiring Pinnacle to arbitrate in Washington before a single arbitrator ' 'imposes cost and inconvenience for no reason related to the matter.', {})], align='j') RT([('The arbitration clause\'s express coverage of malpractice claims, coupled with the jury waiver and the ' '§13 damages cap, means that a claim against the Firm would be heard by one arbitrator, in the Firm\'s ' 'home city, under the Firm\'s chosen law, with recovery limited to $1,000,000. Each element is ' 'defensible in isolation; stacked, they amount to a comprehensive limitation on the client\'s remedies. ' 'The stack, not any single clause, is the objection. Sections 17 and 18 should be replaced with OCG ' '§§13.2 and 14.1.', {})], align='j') H('F. Marketing use of Pinnacle\'s name', 2) RT([('EL §16 has Pinnacle consent to HB&C naming it in marketing materials, on the Firm\'s website, in ' 'client lists and in pitch materials, continuing after the engagement ends unless revoked in writing. ' 'OCG §10.1 provides the opposite default: counsel "may not use Pinnacle\'s name, logo, or the fact of ' 'the engagement for any marketing, advertising, promotional, or business development purpose ... ' 'without the prior written consent of the General Counsel," a restriction that applies both during and ' 'after the engagement. The clause reverses the default and should be struck; any use should require ' 'specific advance written consent.', {})], align='j') RT([('Relatedly, OCG §10.1 prohibits disclosing "the existence or nature of any Pinnacle engagement to any ' 'third party without Pinnacle\'s prior written consent." The CrossPoint proposal recites the matter ' 'caption, the parties, the damages figure, the termination date, the MSA date, and the substance of ' 'Pinnacle\'s defence. Disclosure to a prospective vendor is ordinary and probably unobjectionable, but ' 'it has already occurred, and confirmation that it was consented to should be obtained.', {})], align='j')

content # ===================================================================== # XI. E-DISCOVERY / CROSSPOINT # ===================================================================== H('XI. E-Discovery and the CrossPoint Analytics Engagement') H('A. Vendor approval, sole-sourcing, and the undisclosed economics of the referral', 2) RT([('OCG §1.2 subjects all vendors retained by outside counsel — e-discovery vendors expressly among them — ' 'to the Guidelines, and makes counsel "responsible for ensuring that all such vendors and service ' 'providers comply." It then imposes three requirements that the $380,000 CrossPoint engagement ' 'implicates:', {})], align='j') TBL(['OCG §1.2 requirement', 'Threshold', 'Status'], [ ['Pinnacle\'s prior written approval, with a description of services, the vendor\'s ' 'qualifications, estimated cost, and the basis for selecting the proposed vendor', 'Vendor fees > $25,000', 'Not obtained; $380,000 is 15× the threshold'], ['Pinnacle may require competitive bidding', 'Vendor fees > $50,000', 'No bid process; sole-sourced on relationship'], ['Counsel "must avoid retaining vendors in which the firm or any of its attorneys holds a financial ' 'interest, unless such interest is disclosed in writing and approved by Pinnacle"', 'Any financial interest', 'Unresolved — see below'], ], widths=[3.1, 1.35, 2.05], fontsize=8.5) RT([('The disclosure problem is sharper than a bare "no disclosure" finding, and it is worth stating ' 'precisely. ', {'b': True}), ('EL §7 does not fail to disclose a relationship. It affirmatively discloses that a commercial ' 'partnership exists — CrossPoint is "a strategic partner of the Firm," offering "preferred rates ' 'available through its partnership with the Firm" — and then discloses nothing whatsoever about its ' 'economics. The letter tells the client there is an arrangement, invites the client to rely on the ' 'Firm\'s recommendation of its partner, and never says whether the Firm receives anything. "Preferred ' 'rates available through its partnership with the Firm" reads identically whether the preference is a ' 'pure client benefit or a shared margin.', {})], align='j') RT([('The CrossPoint proposal says the same thing from the other side: it opens by describing CrossPoint as ' '"a long-standing strategic partner of Hawthorne, Bellamy & Cross LLP" that has supported the Firm "on ' 'over forty engagements in the past five years," and states that the preferred rates "are available ' 'exclusively to Hawthorne, Bellamy & Cross LLP engagements." Forty engagements in five years is a ' 'substantial commercial relationship in which Pinnacle is a payer and not a party.', {})], align='j') RT([('Nothing in the record indicates that HB&C receives consideration from CrossPoint, and this memorandum ' 'does not assert or imply that it does. ', {'b': True}), ('The correspondence file contains no reference to CrossPoint, vendors, referral arrangements, rebates, ' 'revenue shares, discounts or commissions of any kind. That is precisely the point: the structure ' 'creates the referral without creating any mechanism by which Pinnacle could learn what the referral is ' 'worth to the Firm. The remedy is a direct written certification, which Section XVIII sets out.', {})], align='j') RT([('Pinnacle should also note OCG §1.2\'s closing sentence: "Pinnacle may, in its sole discretion, direct ' 'outside counsel to use a Pinnacle-preferred vendor for any category of services." On a $380,000 spend, ' 'obtaining two comparative bids is proportionate and is the Guidelines\' expressed expectation above ' '$50,000. Competitive tension on e-discovery pricing of this size commonly yields double-digit ' 'reductions; a 15–30% improvement would be $57,000 to $114,000.', {})], align='j') H('B. The proposal is not subject to the Guidelines and runs to the wrong party', 2) BR([('No incorporation. ', {'b': True}), ('The CrossPoint proposal never references the Outside Counsel Guidelines, consistent with the pattern ' 'across the whole package. Under OCG §1.2 the vendor is subject to them, and HB&C is responsible for ' 'ensuring compliance; the proposal contains nothing to that effect.', {})]) BR([('No privity for Pinnacle. ', {'b': True}), ('"CrossPoint\'s invoicing relationship is with HB&C; CrossPoint will not invoice Pinnacle directly." ' 'Pinnacle bears 100% of a $380,000 cost while holding no direct contractual rights against the vendor ' 'handling its data — including no direct remedy in the event of a breach.', {})]) BR([('Approvals run to HB&C, not Pinnacle. ', {'b': True}), ('CrossPoint will "seek prior authorization from HB&C before incurring any charges against the ' 'contingency allocation that exceed $5,000 individually," and scope expansions are agreed with HB&C. ' 'Under OCG §5.2 that $5,000 approval right belongs to the designated Pinnacle attorney. The approval ' 'chain is pointed at the wrong party throughout.', {})]) BR([('Unilateral rate increases. ', {'b': True}), ('Preferred rates are "subject to annual review and adjustment upon thirty days\' written notice to ' 'HB&C" — no Pinnacle consent required. Rates should be locked for the engagement duration or made ' 'subject to Pinnacle\'s approval.', {})]) BR([('Pass-through of an 18% finance charge. ', {'b': True}), ('Late payments carry 1.5% per month. Interest is not a reimbursable category under the Guidelines, and ' 'passing it through would penalise Pinnacle for HB&C\'s payment timing or for Pinnacle\'s own exercise ' 'of its right to withhold disputed amounts. It should be expressly non-passthrough.', {})]) BR([('The confidentiality legend excludes Pinnacle. ', {'b': True}), ('The proposal is "confidential and intended solely for the use of Hawthorne, Bellamy & Cross LLP," and ' '"[a]ny distribution, reproduction, or disclosure to third parties without the prior written consent of ' 'CrossPoint Analytics is strictly prohibited." On its face the client who pays for the services is a ' 'prohibited recipient. This also sits awkwardly with OCG §7.1. The legend should be revised, or ' 'CrossPoint\'s consent to disclosure to Pinnacle confirmed in writing.', {})]) BR([('Expired on its face. ', {'b': True}), ('The proposal was valid for sixty days, "through December 4, 2025." Any current engagement is ' 'necessarily on re-quoted or superseded terms that have not been reviewed.', {})]) H('C. Two quantitative problems in the estimate', 2) RT([('Setting aside the terms, the $380,000 estimate does not reconcile internally in two respects. Both ' 'should be put to CrossPoint and HB&C before any authorisation, because both are asymmetric: each ' 'understates cost rather than overstating it.', {})], align='j') H('(1) The hosting line implies a far smaller data set than the proposal describes', 3) RT([('Hosting is quoted at $18 per GB per month, with a twelve-month estimate of $48,600. That works out to ' '$4,050 per month, which at $18 per GB implies an average hosted volume of ', {}), ('approximately 225 GB', {'b': True}), ('. But the proposal states a pre-collection volume of 1.2 to 1.8 TB and uses 1.5 TB for the processing ' 'line. Hosting 225 GB assumes an 85% reduction through de-duplication, de-NISTing, date culling and ' 'keyword filtering — an optimistic figure, and one stated nowhere in the proposal.', {})], align='j') TBL(['Culling achieved', 'Hosted volume', 'Monthly hosting', '12-month hosting', 'Variance vs. estimate'], [ ['85% (implied by the estimate)', '225 GB', '$4,050', '$48,600', '—'], ['70%', '450 GB', '$8,100', '$97,200', '+$48,600'], ['60%', '600 GB', '$10,800', '$129,600', '+$81,000'], ], widths=[1.75, 1.15, 1.15, 1.25, 1.2], fontsize=8.5) RT([('A second, smaller point compounds this: hosting accrues on a volume that grows as collections come in, ' 'so a flat twelve-month average understates the later months even if the total volume assumption holds. ' 'Pinnacle should require the culling assumption to be stated expressly, a not-to-exceed on hosting, and ' 'a tiered or declining per-GB rate at higher volumes, which is standard at this scale. OCG §5.2 also ' 'permits blanket approval of recurring charges where the request specifies the nature, estimated ' 'monthly amount and duration — that is the right mechanism here, with a ceiling.', {})], align='j') H('(2) The review platform sizing implies a review effort several times larger than the budget', 3) RT([('This is the more significant of the two, and potentially the largest undisclosed cost exposure in the ' 'entire package.', {'b': True})], align='j') RT([('The "Review Platform & TAR" line is $47,000. Backing out TAR at the quoted $5,000 setup plus $25/GB on ' 'the implied 225 GB — $10,625 — leaves roughly $36,375 for platform licences at $45 per user per month. ' 'That is about 808 user-months: on a twelve-month engagement, roughly ', {}), ('67 concurrent reviewer seats', {'b': True}), ('. ', {'b': True}), ('This is presented as a question rather than a conclusion — the answer turns on TAR efficacy, the ' 'scope of the search-term protocol ultimately agreed at the Rule 26(f) conference, and whether the ' 'parties negotiate a TAR-based production protocol. Note also that $8,500 per month exceeds the OCG ' '§5.2 $5,000 single-expense threshold, so each monthly charge requires approval absent a blanket ' 'authorisation.', {})]) BR([('Processing reconciles. ', {'b': True}), ('1,500 GB at $35 per GB is $52,500, matching the estimate. No issue.', {})]) BR([('No exit costs are quoted. ', {'b': True}), ('The proposal contains no data egress, export or return pricing, no data disposition schedule, and no ' 'certified destruction obligation. Export costs at the end of a hosted engagement are a common and ' 'sometimes substantial hidden charge, and their absence should not be read as their being free.', {})]) BR([('No vendor lien prohibition. Given OCG §7.2 and the ' 'realistic prospect of a payment dispute somewhere in a twelve-month engagement, an express no-lien ' 'covenant plus a guaranteed data-return obligation should be required. CrossPoint\'s limitation of liability, viewed from Pinnacle\'s position', 2) RT([('CrossPoint\'s aggregate liability is capped at the fees paid in the preceding twelve months — roughly ' '$380,000 — with all consequential, incidental, indirect, special and punitive damages excluded, ' '"including but not limited to lost profits, ', {}), ('loss of data', {'i': True}), (', or business ' 'interruption."', {})], align='j') RT([('For a vendor taking custody of 1.2 to 1.8 terabytes of a health system\'s data, including mailboxes ' 'across clinical, IT, compliance and legal functions, an express exclusion for loss of data is a ' 'material term. Pinnacle bears the residual risk, has no privity through which to negotiate, and — ' 'under the engagement letter as drafted — would find its recourse against HB&C capped at $1,000,000 as ' 'well. Pinnacle should require: designation as a third-party beneficiary or a direct agreement with ' 'CrossPoint; carve-outs from the cap for breach of confidentiality or data security, for any PHI ' 'incident, and for gross negligence and wilful misconduct; and cyber and technology errors-and-omissions ' 'coverage commensurate with the data volume, with evidence of coverage provided.', {})], align='j') # ===================================================================== # XII. The engagement letter has a general confidentiality clause ' 'at §16 but imposes no information-security requirements, no breach-notification obligation, and no ' 'HIPAA or business-associate terms — on a healthcare client whose underlying dispute, as §1 of the ' 'letter itself recites, involves "data integrity failures that compromised patient record accuracy."', {})], align='j') RT([('OCG §10.2 requires counsel to encrypt communications containing Pinnacle confidential information, ' 'use secure access-controlled file sharing, restrict access on a need-to-know basis, comply with HIPAA ' 'and HITECH, and — critically — "[n]otify the General Counsel in writing within twenty-four (24) hours ' 'of discovering any actual or suspected data breach, unauthorized access, or security incident ' 'involving Pinnacle information." None of this appears in the engagement letter, and the 24-hour ' 'notification obligation appears nowhere in any of the three documents.', {})], align='j') H('B. CrossPoint\'s security posture is sound but its obligations do not run to Pinnacle', 2) RT([('CrossPoint represents SOC 2 Type II certification, AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, ' 'US-based data centres, multi-factor access controls, continuous monitoring, and background checks for ' 'technical personnel. That is a credible baseline and compares well against OCG §10.2. The gaps are ' 'contractual rather than technical:', {})], align='j') BR([('No breach notification obligation of any kind', {'b': True}), (' — not at 24 hours, not at any interval, and not to anyone. This is the most important single addition ' 'required, and it must run directly to Pinnacle\'s General Counsel, not solely to HB&C, and must flow ' 'down to any CrossPoint subcontractor.', {})]) BR([('The BAA is conditional. ', {'b': True}), ('CrossPoint "will execute a Business Associate Agreement if required." Given that the collection scope ' 'covers EHR integration platform data, system logs, and mailboxes belonging to clinical, IT and ' 'compliance personnel across a health system, the presence of protected health information is close to ' 'certain rather than contingent. Executed BAAs should be required with both HB&C and CrossPoint, ' 'before any collection begins, with Pinnacle as the covered entity party. HITECH\'s 60-day breach ' 'notification floor should be expressly displaced by the OCG\'s 24-hour requirement.', {})]) BR([('The NDA excludes Pinnacle. ', {'b': True}), ('The proposal contemplates "a mutual non-disclosure agreement" between CrossPoint and HB&C. Pinnacle — ' 'whose confidential information and patient data are the entire subject matter — is not a party and is ' 'protected only derivatively.', {})]) BR([('No security questionnaire or assessment right. ', {'b': True}), ('OCG §10.2 reserves Pinnacle\'s right to require a data security questionnaire and to conduct periodic ' 'assessments. That right should be extended expressly to CrossPoint.', {})]) H('C. Collecting in-house counsel mailboxes in a matter of ' 'this size is sometimes necessary, but it carries real waiver risk, and ', {}), ('nothing in any of the three documents addresses privilege protection.', {'b': True}), (' Specifically, there is no reference to a Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) order, no clawback ' 'agreement, no ESI protocol, no privilege screening workflow, and no privilege log methodology.', {})], align='j') RT([('The timing is favourable if acted on. The Rule 26(f) conference is the natural vehicle for both a ' '502(d) order and an agreed ESI protocol, and CrossPoint\'s own proposal notes that the parties will be ' 'expected to address ESI preservation, collection and production there. content # ===================================================================== # XIII. PROFESSIONAL RESPONSIBILITY # ===================================================================== H('XIII. Professional Responsibility Observations') RT([('The following are flagged because they bear on whether terms in the proposed letter are enforceable at ' 'all, which affects how Pinnacle should negotiate them. They are raised as issues for confirmation, not ' 'as conclusions. Each turns on which jurisdiction\'s rules apply — itself contested here, since the ' 'letter selects District of Columbia law for a North Carolina matter — and each should be confirmed by ' 'counsel admitted in the relevant jurisdiction before being asserted to the Firm.', {})], align='j') H('A. The prospective malpractice limitation (EL §13) and the indemnity (EL §14)', 2) RT([('Rules of professional conduct in most jurisdictions restrict prospective limitations of a lawyer\'s ' 'malpractice liability to a client. The ABA Model Rule formulation, followed in North Carolina, permits ' 'such an agreement only where the client is independently represented in making it. The District of ' 'Columbia\'s rule is stricter and, as generally understood, prohibits prospective limitation outright.', {})], align='j') RT([('Two observations follow. ', {'b': True}), ('First, EL §20(b) — the acknowledgment that the Client "has had the opportunity to consult with ' 'independent counsel regarding these terms" — appears designed to satisfy the ' 'independent-representation predicate. It probably does not: an ', {}), ('opportunity to consult', {'i': True}), (' is not the same as being ', {}), ('independently represented in making the agreement', {'i': True}), (', and in a jurisdiction with a flat prohibition no acknowledgment would cure it. Second, the letter ' 'selects D.C. law at §18 and D.C. arbitration at §17 — so on the Firm\'s own choice-of-law clause, the ' 'stricter rule is the one in play.', {})], align='j') RT([('EL §14 raises the same concern in substance. An indemnity that requires the client to hold the firm ' 'harmless for the firm\'s own negligence achieves by indemnification what §13 achieves by cap, and is ' 'generally analysed the same way.', {})], align='j') H('B. Arbitration of malpractice claims (EL §17)', 2) RT([('An agreement to arbitrate malpractice claims is not impermissible as such, but the prevailing view — ' 'reflected in ABA Formal Opinion 02-425 — is that it requires the client to be fully informed of the ' 'scope and effect of the clause, and that it may not be used to insulate the lawyer from liability ' 'that would otherwise be available. Here the clause appears at §17 of a twenty-section letter, carries ' 'a jury-trial waiver, expressly extends to malpractice, and operates together with the §13 cap. Whether ' 'the informed-consent standard is met by a form clause presented in that posture is at least ' 'questionable.', {})], align='j') H('C. The retainer (EL §4)', 2) RT([('An advance fee deposited directly into a firm\'s operating account and designated "earned upon ' 'receipt" attracts scrutiny under the trust-accounting rules in most jurisdictions. The label is not ' 'conclusive; the question is generally whether the fee was in substance earned when paid and whether ' 'the arrangement is reasonable. A $250,000 non-refundable payment made at the outset of a litigation ' 'defence, retained in full even if the engagement terminates immediately, is the paradigm case for that ' 'scrutiny. Independently, OCG §3.6 requires deposit into the client trust account, which resolves the ' 'point as a contractual matter if the Guidelines apply.', {})], align='j') H('D. Impediments to discharging counsel (EL §§4, 9, 15)', 2) RT([('A client\'s right to discharge counsel is generally treated as near-absolute, with counsel\'s ' 'entitlement on discharge limited to reasonable value for services rendered. The proposed structure ' 'layers three impediments on that right: a $250,000 non-refundable retainer, a 15% termination fee ' 'payable on any client-initiated termination, and a retaining lien over the file until all invoices are ' 'paid. Individually each is a term to negotiate; together they impose a substantial financial penalty ' 'on the exercise of the right and, through the lien, a practical obstacle to transitioning the matter ' 'at all. OCG §8.1 reaches the same result contractually by declaring termination fees void.', {})], align='j') H('E. Contract attorney billing (EL §2)', 2) RT([('Under the generally accepted framework — ABA Formal Opinion 00-420 — a firm may bill contract lawyer ' 'services as a fee subject to the overall reasonableness requirement, or pass them through as a cost at ' 'actual cost, but it may not present a marked-up charge as a disbursement. The engagement letter is ' 'silent on which treatment applies and contains no at-cost or no-markup language. Where the permitted ' 'rate is $350 per hour and agency cost for document review is typically a fraction of that, the ' 'difference between the two treatments across 750 to 1,000 hours — or the far larger volumes Section ' 'XI.C suggests — is material. Pinnacle should require pass-through at cost with the underlying invoices ' 'available, or a rate at the OCG §6.3 cap.', {})], align='j') H('F. The conflicts position', 2) RT([('Section IV addresses this at length. The professional-responsibility dimension is that informed ' 'consent to a conflict requires disclosure of the material facts, and that an advance waiver of ' 'unknown future conflicts — even one valid as against a sophisticated client — cannot supply consent to ' 'a specific conflict that was identified before execution and then omitted from the operative document. ' 'EL §11 ¶1 represents that no conflicts exist; EL §19 disclaims the emails in which the conflict was ' 'disclosed. Whatever else it does, that combination does not produce informed consent.', {})], align='j') # ===================================================================== # XIV. OPERATIONAL SILENCES # ===================================================================== H('XIV. Operational Requirements on Which the Engagement Letter Is Silent') RT([('The following OCG obligations have no counterpart anywhere in the engagement letter, its exhibits, the ' 'staffing plan, or the CrossPoint proposal. Each was searched for specifically. These are silences, not ' 'conflicts — but the Guidelines make them mandatory, and given the §19 integration clause a silence in ' 'the letter is not obviously filled by the Guidelines. They should be captured in a single compliance ' 'addendum rather than negotiated individually.', {})], align='j') TBL(['Requirement', 'OCG', 'Status in the package'], [ ['LEDES 1998B format via Pinnacle\'s e-billing platform', '§3.4', 'Silent — "electronically" only'], ['Six-word minimum task narratives; block billing prohibited', '§3.4(b)', 'Silent'], ['Cumulative budget-to-actual comparison on every invoice', '§3.4(f)', 'Silent'], ['Supporting documentation for expenses above $250', '§3.4(e)', 'Silent'], ['Monthly written status reports within 10 business days of month-end', '§11.1', 'Silent — no case status reporting of any frequency'], ['24-hour notice of significant developments (dispositive motions, settlement demands, adverse ' 'rulings, sanctions, regulatory inquiries)', '§11.2', 'Silent'], ['Quarterly budget updates within 15 days of quarter-end', '§4.2', 'Partial — quarterly, no deadline stated'], ['Immediate notice and written approval at 10% budget variance', '§4.2', 'Silent'], ['Quarterly diversity reports within 30 days of quarter-end', '§6.4', 'Silent'], ['Designated Pinnacle attorney as primary contact; prior written approval for settlement authority, ' 'strategy, motion practice and expert retention', '§11.3', 'Silent — no client-side contact designated; firm-side contacts only'], ['Annual insurance updates and proof on request', '§2.3', 'Silent'], ['Right to audit invoices, time records and expense reports', '§12.1', 'Silent — no audit right'], ['Pinnacle matter name and matter number on each invoice', '§§2.1(a), 3.4(a)', 'No matter number appears anywhere'], ['Vendor approval gate for third-party retentions generally', '§1.2', 'Silent; §6\'s $15,000 gate and §7\'s e-discovery pass-through are in unresolved tension'], ['Travel time billability and rate', '§5.3 (by implication)', 'Silent'], ['Minimum billing increments', '§3.4', 'Silent'], ['Designation of any task as non-billable overhead', '§5.4', 'Silent — billing review is assigned to a partner at $975/hr'], ['Data security, breach notification, HIPAA / BAA terms', '§10.2', 'Silent in the letter; conditional in the CrossPoint proposal'], ], widths=[2.85, 0.72, 2.93], fontsize=8.2) RT([('Two of these deserve emphasis. The absence of any ', {}), ('case status reporting', {'b': True}), (' obligation means that, as drafted, Pinnacle would receive a budget summary once a quarter and nothing ' 'else — no development reports, no early case assessment, no written litigation plan, and no obligation ' 'to report an adverse ruling or a settlement demand. And the absence of any ', {}), ('audit right', {'b': True}), (' removes the mechanism OCG §12.1 relies on to make every other billing provision enforceable.', {})], align='j') # ===================================================================== # XV. INCONSISTENCIES # ===================================================================== H('XV. Internal Inconsistencies and Diligence Items') RT([('These are minor relative to the foregoing, but several suggest that parts of the package were ' 'assembled from precedent without close checking, which is itself worth knowing when assessing the ' 'care behind the substantive terms.', {})], align='j') TBL(['#', 'Item', 'Detail'], [ ['1', 'The presiding judge is named differently in two documents', 'The staffing plan identifies "the Honorable Malcolm R. Drummond." The CrossPoint proposal ' 'identifies "the Honorable Judge M.R. Desmond." Same case number, 3:25-cv-01847-MRD. One is wrong.'], ['2', 'HB&C\'s own address differs between documents', 'The staffing plan letterhead reads 301 South Tryon Street, Suite 2400, Charlotte, NC 28202. ' 'CrossPoint addresses HB&C at 1200 West Morehead Street, Suite 2400, Charlotte, NC 28208.'], ['3', 'No Pinnacle matter number anywhere', 'Required by OCG §2.1(a) in the engagement letter and by §3.4(a) on every invoice. Absent from all ' 'three documents.'], ['4', 'The staffing plan attributes a term to the engagement letter that the letter does not contain', 'Staffing plan §3 refers to contract attorney time billed "in accordance with the standard billing ' 'practices outlined in the Engagement Letter." The letter contains no such provision — only a bare ' 'rate permission at §2 and the Exhibit A line.'], ['5', 'The blended rate election is described inconsistently', 'The staffing plan presents it as available "at the Client\'s election." EL §3.2 requires the ' 'election to be made at execution and marked below the signature block — a one-time choice, not a ' 'continuing right.'], ['6', 'CrossPoint\'s signature block names a middle initial not used elsewhere', '"Sandra K. Morrow / James D. Alcott." The staffing plan and both emails use "James Alcott."'], ['7', 'CrossPoint proposal expired on its face', 'Valid sixty days, "through December 4, 2025."'], ['8', 'Custodian count differs between scope and pricing', 'Scope says 35–50 custodians; the cost estimate prices 45, at the top of the range.'], ['9', 'Phase 1 and Phase 2 overlap by three months', 'Phase 1 runs Nov 2025 – Sept 2026; Phase 2 begins July 2026. Not improper, but phase-level ' 'budget-to-actual reporting must account for it.'], ['10', 'The staffing plan\'s arithmetic is correct', 'Noted affirmatively: every phase subtotal, every timekeeper total, the 1,880-hour and $1,141,500 ' 'grand totals, and the four phase targets summing to $2,400,000 all reconcile exactly. No ' 'computational errors were found.'], ], widths=[0.32, 2.15, 4.03], fontsize=8.2)

contentSam — memo is filed as engagement-review-memo.docx. Closing the loop, since your material carried most of it. Your correction landed before I drafted. The finding is stated the way you framed it: the October 4 email names MedBridge in its second sentence and is expressly the promised follow-up, but the search scope it recites (NovaTech, its principals, Prescott Lane) does not reach MedBridge, MedBridge's own matters, or NovaTech's equity holders, and it returns an unqualified "no issues" without restating or analysing the 8% stake. So it presents as responsive while not performing the analysis the disclosure called for. I did not use "never mentions MedBridge" anywhere. What your material changed structurally: the lead finding is no longer the rate caps, it is that the OCG is never referenced in the engagement letter and §19 is a full integration clause. I ran your search against my two documents as you suggested — the staffing plan and the CrossPoint proposal contain no OCG reference either. So the Guidelines appear nowhere across the entire HB&C-side package. That reframed the memo: every other finding is a conflict between the letter and the Guidelines, and each presupposes the Guidelines apply. I took your recommendations on framing in three places. Execution status is written as pre-execution with an explicit standing assumption that non-execution is confirmed only through October 4, 2025, plus your list of what changes character if it was in fact signed. The OCG-transmittal point is posed as a directed question to Ridley or Yeun rather than resolved by inference, with your reasoning that your file is one-directional and close to the worst place to look. And the CrossPoint disclosure finding is written your way — §7 does not fail to disclose a relationship, it discloses that a partnership exists and then discloses nothing about its economics. The memo does not assert or imply that HB&C receives consideration; it asks for a certification. Your provenance note on the Morrow email is a footnote in Section II.B recommending the original be pulled from Pinnacle's mail system before it is used as an exhibit. Two things I found on my side that you could not have seen, both in the vendor package, and both cutting the same direction: The CrossPoint hosting line prices out to about 225 GB of average hosted volume, against a stated 1.2–1.8 TB collection. That implies an 85% culling rate stated nowhere in the proposal. At 70% culling, hosting roughly doubles. More seriously, the review platform and TAR line implies roughly 67 concurrent reviewer seats, while the staffing plan budgets 750–1,000 contract attorney hours in total. Working from the document side gives the same mismatch: 350,000–500,000 documents at normal first-pass rates is 7,000–10,000 review hours, and even aggressive TAR leaves 1,400–2,000. The contract attorney estimate looks understated by somewhere between two and ten times, inside a Phase 1 allocation that reserves $262,500–$350,000 for it, inside a budget that is expressly not a cap, under a letter granting sole staffing discretion. That may be the largest undisclosed exposure in the package, and it is written as a question rather than a conclusion. No further ask. Recording the item complete now. — Morgan

outcomeFiled /media/user/data/work/output/engagement-review-memo.docx — a comprehensive issues memo reviewing the proposed HB&C engagement letter, staffing plan, and CrossPoint e-discovery proposal against Pinnacle's Outside Counsel Guidelines (Jan 2024). 47 pages, 18 sections plus a clause-by-clause OCG compliance matrix. Recommendation: do not execute as drafted. Threshold findings: (1) The OCG is never referenced anywhere in the HB&C-side package — engagement letter, exhibits, staffing plan, or vendor proposal — and EL §19 is a full integration clause, giving HB&C a serious argument the Guidelines do not apply at all; correcting this resolves most other issues. (2) Unresolved conflict — HB&C represents MedBridge Therapeutics, holder of ~8% of adverse party NovaTech, squarely within the OCG's 5% "material financial interest" trigger; the promised formal clearance was never delivered as to that issue, consent went to the AGC rather than the GC as required, EL §11 represents no conflicts exist, and EL §11 ¶2 is a prohibited blanket advance waiver. Also identified MedBridge as a likely third-party discovery target on Pinnacle's own material-breach defence. Quantified ~$559,000–$600,000 in non-contingent excess cost plus up to ~$1.65M contingent (success fee up to $1,420,000 payable on dismissal; 15% termination fee), against a $2.4M budget expressly "not a cap" — total potential $4.45M, or 31% of the $14.2M pleaded demand. Every timekeeper rate is above cap; insurance is $10M/$20M against a mandatory $25M/$50M; malpractice liability capped at the lesser of $1M or fees paid; client indemnifies the firm for its own negligence; retaining lien asserted; $250,000 non-refundable retainer into the firm's operating account. Two original quantitative findings in the vendor package: hosting pricing implies ~225 GB against a stated 1.2–1.8 TB collection (an unstated 85% culling assumption), and the review-platform sizing implies ~67 reviewer seats against a budgeted 750–1,000 contract attorney hours — suggesting review volume is understated by 2–10x. Memo includes 22 directed questions (internal, to HB&C, and to HB&C/CrossPoint jointly), a prioritised remediation table covering 19 engagement letter sections, and explicit sourcing and execution-status limitations: the engagement letter was not staged for review and its terms are reported second-hand from the correspondence file, and non-execution is confirmed only through October 4, 2025.

I sent the five terms they asked about verbatim, plus the provisions they had no visibility into — the $250K non-refundable retainer, a 15% termination fee, a success fee that pays out *maximum* on a dismissal ($1.42M at a $0 outcome), a liability cap of the lesser of $1M or fees paid, client indemnification of the firm's own negligence, mandatory arbitration of malpractice, and a retaining lien.\n\n**Two things worth flagging to you:**\n\n1. **I had to correct myself.** In my first message I wrote that Alcott's clearance email \"does not mention MedBridge at all.\" It does — in its second sentence. Morgan had said this would be their lead finding and that they intended to quote it, so I led the second message with the correction and gave them the accurate, narrower version: the email is *framed* as the MedBridge follow-up but describes a search scoped only to NovaTech, its principals, and opposing counsel, and returns an unqualified clearance without analyzing the 8% equity stake. Still a finding — but not the one I originally described.\n\n2. **The conflicts sequence is the real issue in this file.** Morrow disclosed on Oct 3 that HB&C represents MedBridge, that MedBridge holds ~8% of NovaTech, promised a formal conflicts-team confirmation, and noted the firm was already doing substantive work pre-execution. What arrived was a partner email, not a conflicts-team memo.
